الْجُزْءُ الْعَاشِرُ
كِتَابُ عِلْمِ الْسُلُوكِ
قَالَ شَيْخُ الْإِسْلَامِ أَحْمَد ابْنُ تَيْمِيَّة - قَدَّسَ اللَّهُ رُوحَهُ -:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَحْدَهُ وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى مَنْ لَا نَبِيَّ بَعْدَهُ. الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ نَسْتَعِينُهُ وَنَسْتَغْفِرُهُ وَنَعُوذُ بِاَللَّهِ مِنْ شُرُورِ أَنْفُسِنَا وَمِنْ سَيِّئَاتِ أَعْمَالِنَا مَنْ يَهْدِهِ اللَّهُ فَلَا مُضِلَّ لَهُ وَمَنْ يُضْلِلْ فَلَا هَادِيَ لَهُ وَنَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إلَهَ إلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَنَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ. صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ وَسَلَّمَ.
أَمَّا بَعْدُ:
فَهَذِهِ كَلِمَاتٌ مُخْتَصَرَاتٌ فِي أَعْمَالِ الْقُلُوبِ - الَّتِي قَدْ تُسَمَّى 
" الْمَقَامَاتِ وَالْأَحْوَالَ "
 - وَهِيَ مِنْ أُصُولِ الْإِيمَانِ وَقَوَاعِدِ الدِّينِ؛ مِثْلُ
translated_text:
Volume Ten
Book of the Science of Spiritual Conduct

Shaykh al-Islām Ahmad ibn Taymiyya—may Allah sanctify his soul—said:

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

Praise be to Allah alone, and blessings and peace be upon the one after whom there is no prophet.

All praise is due to Allah. We seek His help and forgiveness, and we seek refuge in Allah from the evil within ourselves and from our evil deeds. Whoever Allah guides, none can lead astray; and whoever He leads astray, none can guide. We bear witness that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone, without partner, and we bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. May Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace.

To proceed:

These are a few brief remarks on the deeds of the heart—sometimes called “stations and states”—which are among the foundations of faith and the pillars of religion, such as

original_text:
مَحَبَّةِ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَالتَّوَكُّلِ عَلَى اللَّهِ وَإِخْلَاصِ الدِّينِ لَهُ وَالشُّكْرِ لَهُ وَالصَّبْرِ عَلَى حُكْمِهِ وَالْخَوْفِ مِنْهُ وَالرَّجَاءِ لَهُ وَمَا يَتْبَعُ ذَلِكَ. اقْتَضَى ذَلِكَ بَعْضُ مَنْ أَوْجَبَ اللَّهُ حَقَّهُ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْإِيمَانِ وَاسْتَكْتَبَهَا وَكُلٌّ مِنَّا عَجْلَانُ.
 فَأَقُولُ:
 هَذِهِ الْأَعْمَالُ جَمِيعُهَا وَاجِبَةٌ عَلَى جَمِيعِ الْخَلْقِ - الْمَأْمُورِينَ فِي الْأَصْلِ - بِاتِّفَاقِ أَئِمَّةِ الدِّينِ وَالنَّاسُ فِيهَا عَلَى 
" ثَلَاثِ دَرَجَاتٍ "
 كَمَا هُمْ فِي أَعْمَالِ الْأَبْدَانِ عَلَى 
" ثَلَاثِ دَرَجَاتٍ "
: ظَالِمٌ لِنَفْسِهِ وَمُقْتَصِدٌ وَسَابِقٌ بِالْخَيْرَاتِ.
 فَالظَّالِمُ لِنَفْسِهِ:
 الْعَاصِي بِتَرْكِ مَأْمُورٍ أَوْ فِعْلِ مَحْظُورٍ.
 وَالْمُقْتَصِدُ:
 الْمُؤَدِّي الْوَاجِبَاتِ وَالتَّارِكُ الْمُحَرَّمَاتِ.
 وَالسَّابِقُ بِالْخَيْرَاتِ:
 الْمُتَقَرِّبُ بِمَا يَقْدِرُ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ فِعْلِ وَاجِبٍ وَمُسْتَحَبٍّ وَالتَّارِكُ لَلْمُحَرَّمِ وَالْمَكْرُوهِ.
 وَإِنْ كَانَ كُلٌّ مِنْ الْمُقْتَصِدِ وَالسَّابِقِ قَدْ يَكُونُ لَهُ ذُنُوبٌ تُمْحَى عَنْهُ:
 إمَّا بِتَوْبَةِ - وَاَللَّهُ يُحِبُّ التَّوَّابِينَ وَيُحِبُّ الْمُتَطَهِّرِينَ - وَإِمَّا بِحَسَنَاتِ مَاحِيَةٍ وَإِمَّا بِمَصَائِبَ مُكَفِّرَةٍ وَإِمَّا بِغَيْرِ ذَلِكَ.
 وَكُلٌّ مِنْ الصِّنْفَيْنِ الْمُقْتَصِدِينَ وَالسَّابِقِينَ مِنْ أَوْلِيَاءِ اللَّهِ الَّذِينَ ذَكَرَهُمْ فِي كِتَابِهِ بِقَوْلِهِ:
 
{أَلَا إنَّ أَوْلِيَاءَ اللَّهِ لَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ}
 
{الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَكَانُوا يَتَّقُونَ}
 فَحَدُّ أَوْلِيَاءِ اللَّهِ: هُمْ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الْمُتَّقُونَ وَلَكِنَّ ذَلِكَ يَنْقَسِمُ: إلَى 
" عَامٍّ "
 وَهُمْ الْمُقْتَصِدُونَ،
translated_text:
love for Allah and His Messenger, reliance upon Allah, sincere devotion to Him alone, gratitude to Him, patience with His decree, fear of Him, hope in Him, and related matters. One of the believers whose rights Allah has made binding requested these remarks and asked me to write them down, while both of us were pressed for time.

I say:

All these deeds are obligatory upon all created beings—those who are, in principle, subject to divine commands—by the consensus of the leading scholars of religion. People fall into “three ranks” with regard to these deeds, just as they fall into “three ranks” with regard to bodily deeds: those who wrong themselves, those who follow a middle course, and those who are foremost in good deeds.

Those who wrong themselves are those who sin by neglecting something commanded or doing something forbidden.

Those who follow a middle course fulfil their obligations and refrain from prohibited acts.

Those who are foremost in good deeds draw near to Allah by performing whatever obligatory and recommended deeds they can, and by refraining from prohibited and disliked acts.

Nevertheless, both those who follow a middle course and those who are foremost may have sins that are erased: through repentance—and Allah loves those who repent and those who purify themselves—or through good deeds that erase sins, afflictions that expiate them, or other means.

Both groups—those who follow a middle course and those who are foremost—are among the friends of Allah whom He mentions in His Book, saying:

“Indeed, the friends of Allah will have no fear, nor will they grieve.”

“Those who believe and are mindful of Him.”

Thus, the friends of Allah are defined as the believers who are mindful of Him. This, however, is divided into a “general” category, comprising those who follow a middle course,

وَ 
" خَاصٍّ "
 وَهُمْ السَّابِقُونَ وَإِنْ كَانَ السَّابِقُونَ هُمْ أَعْلَى دَرَجَاتٍ كَالْأَنْبِيَاءِ وَالصِّدِّيقِينَ. وَقَدْ ذَكَرَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ وَسَلَّمَ 
" الْقِسْمَيْنِ "

 .
 وَأَمَّا الظَّالِمُ لِنَفْسِهِ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْإِيمَانِ:
 فَمَعَهُ مِنْ وِلَايَةِ اللَّهِ بِقَدْرِ إيمَانِهِ وَتَقْوَاهُ كَمَا مَعَهُ مِنْ ضِدِّ ذَلِكَ بِقَدْرِ فُجُورِهِ إذْ الشَّخْصُ الْوَاحِدُ قَدْ يَجْتَمِعُ فِيهِ الْحَسَنَاتُ الْمُقْتَضِيَةُ لِلثَّوَابِ وَالسَّيِّئَاتُ الْمُقْتَضِيَةُ لِلْعِقَابِ حَتَّى يُمْكِنَ أَنْ يُثَابَ وَيُعَاقَبَ وَهَذَا قَوْلُ جَمِيعِ أَصْحَابِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَأَئِمَّةِ الْإِسْلَامِ وَأَهْلِ السُّنَّةِ وَالْجَمَاعَةِ الَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ: إنَّهُ لَا يُخَلَّدُ فِي النَّارِ مَنْ فِي قَلْبِهِ مِثْقَالُ ذَرَّةٍ مِنْ إيمَانٍ.
translated_text:
and a “special” category, comprising those who are foremost, although those who are foremost—such as the prophets and the utterly truthful—are higher in rank.

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, mentioned these “two categories” in the hadith narrated by al-Bukhārī in his Sahīh from Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, who said:

“Allah says: ‘Whoever shows enmity towards a friend of Mine has openly challenged Me to war. My servant draws near to Me through nothing like fulfilling what I have made obligatory upon him. My servant continues to draw near to Me through voluntary deeds until I love him. When I love him, I become his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he grasps, and his foot with which he walks. Through Me he hears, through Me he sees, through Me he grasps, and through Me he walks. If he asks Me, I will surely give him, and if he seeks My protection, I will surely protect him. I have never hesitated over anything I am to do as I hesitate over taking the soul of My believing servant: he dislikes death, and I dislike causing him distress, yet he must undergo it.’”

As for a believer who wrongs himself, he has a share of friendship with Allah commensurate with his faith and mindfulness of Him, just as he has a share of its opposite commensurate with his wickedness. A single person may combine good deeds that merit reward with evil deeds that merit punishment, so that he may be both rewarded and punished. This is the position of all the Companions of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, the leading scholars of Islam, and the adherents of the Sunnah and the community, who affirm that no one with an atom’s weight of faith in his heart will remain in the Fire forever.

 يَحْقِرُ
translated_text:
As for those who maintain that such people remain eternally in the Fire—such as the Khawārij and the Muʿtazilah, who hold that no one among the people of the qiblah who enters the Fire will ever leave it, and that neither the Messenger nor anyone else can intercede for those guilty of major sins, whether before or after they enter the Fire—they maintain that a single person cannot combine reward and punishment, or good deeds and evil deeds. Rather, whoever is rewarded is not punished, and whoever is punished is not rewarded.

The evidence for this principle from the Quran, the Sunnah, and the consensus of the early generations of the Muslim community is abundant. This is not the place to discuss it; we have explained it at length in its appropriate places. Many matters follow from this. Thus, whoever possesses genuine faith must possess a measure of these deeds proportionate to his faith, even if he has sins. As al-Bukhārī narrated in his Sahīh from ʿUmar ibn al-Khattāb, may Allah be pleased with him:

“There was a man nicknamed Himār who used to make the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, laugh. He would drink wine, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would have him flogged. Once, when he was brought forward, a man said, ‘May Allah curse him! How often he is brought before the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace!’ The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to him, ‘Do not curse him, for he loves Allah and His Messenger.’”

This shows that someone who sins by drinking or otherwise may nevertheless love Allah and His Messenger, and love for Allah and His Messenger is the strongest bond of faith. Likewise, a devout ascetic may incur the displeasure of Allah and His Messenger on account of the religious innovation and hypocrisy in his heart, in that respect. This is related through numerous reports in the Sahīh collections and elsewhere, from the Commander of the Faithful, ʿAlī ibn Abī Tālib, Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, and others, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, who mentioned the Khawārij and said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, also said concerning them in an authentic hadith:

“A group will break away at a time of division among the Muslims. The nearer of the two factions to the truth will kill them.”

For this reason, leading scholars of Islam, such as Sufyān al-Thawrī and others, said that religious innovation is dearer to Iblīs than sin, because religious innovation is not repented of, whereas sin is repented of.

What they mean by saying that religious innovation is not repented of is that someone who introduces an innovation, adopting as religion something that neither Allah nor His Messenger has prescribed, has had his evil deed made appealing to him, so that he regards it as good. He therefore does not repent as long as he regards it as good. Repentance begins with recognizing that one’s action is evil, so that one may repent of it; or recognizing that one has neglected a good deed commanded as obligatory or recommended, so that one may repent and perform it. As long as he regards his action as good, although it is in fact evil, he does not repent.

Nevertheless, repentance from it is possible and does occur: Allah may guide him and direct him until the truth becomes clear to him, just as He, glorified and exalted is He, has guided those whom He has guided among the disbelievers, the hypocrites, and groups among the people of

religious innovation and misguidance. This comes about by following whatever truth one knows. Whoever acts upon what he knows, Allah grants him knowledge of what he did not know, as He, exalted is He, says:

“As for those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and grants them their piety.”

He, exalted is He, also says:

“If they had done what they were instructed to do, it would have been better for them and would have strengthened them more firmly. Then We would have granted them a great reward from Us and guided them to a straight path.”

He, exalted is He, also says:

“O you who believe, fear Allah and believe in His Messenger. He will grant you a double share of His mercy, provide you with a light by which to walk, and forgive you. And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.”

He, exalted is He, also says:

“Allah is the Protector of those who believe. He brings them out of darkness into the light.”

He, exalted is He, also says:

“There has come to you from Allah a light and a clear Book, through which Allah guides those who seek His pleasure to the paths of peace, brings them out of darkness into the light by His permission, and guides them to a straight path.”

There is abundant evidence for this in the Quran and the Sunnah.

Likewise, whoever turns away from following the truth he knows, in pursuit of his own desires, thereby brings ignorance and misguidance upon himself, until his heart becomes blind to the clear truth. As He, exalted is He, says:

He, exalted is He, also says:

He, exalted is He, also says:

a categorical assertion that, if it came, they would not believe, and that We turn their hearts and eyes away, just as they did not believe in it the first time.

Hence some of the early generations, such as Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, said: “Part of the reward for a good deed is another good deed that follows it, and part of the punishment for an evil deed is another evil deed that follows it.”

It is authentically reported in the two Sahīh collections, from Ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Adhere to truthfulness, for truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise. A man continues to speak the truth and strive to be truthful until he is recorded with Allah as utterly truthful. Beware of lying, for lying leads to wickedness, and wickedness leads to the Fire. A man continues to lie and deliberately pursue falsehood until he is recorded with Allah as a habitual liar.”

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, thus explained that truthfulness is a foundation that necessarily leads to righteousness, and that lying necessarily leads to wickedness. Allah, exalted is He, says:

“Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss, and indeed, the wicked will be in a blazing Fire.”

For this reason, when some religious teachers instructed a follower to repent and wished neither to alienate him nor to divide his attention, they would instruct him to be truthful.

This is also why truthfulness and sincerity were mentioned so frequently in the words of religious teachers and leaders, to the point that they would say: “Tell anyone who is not truthful not to follow me.”

They would also say: “Truthfulness is Allah’s sword on earth: whatever it is brought to bear upon, it cuts through.” Yūsuf ibn Asbāt and others would say: “No servant is ever true to Allah without Allah acting in his favor.” There are many similar sayings.

Truthfulness and sincerity are, in reality, the true realization of faith and Islam, for

those who outwardly profess Islam are divided into believers and hypocrites. What distinguishes the believer from the hypocrite is truthfulness, for lying is the foundation upon which hypocrisy is built. Thus, when Allah describes true faith, He characterizes it by truthfulness, as in His words, exalted is He:

“The Bedouins say, ‘We believe.’ Say, ‘You have not believed; rather, say, “We have submitted.”’”

Up to His words:

“The believers are only those who believe in Allah and His Messenger, then never doubt, and strive with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah. It is they who are truthful.”

He also says, exalted is He:

“For the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes and deprived of their property, seeking bounty from Allah and His pleasure, and supporting Allah and His Messenger. It is they who are truthful.”

He thus declares that those who are truthful in their claim to faith are the believers whose faith is not subsequently overtaken by doubt and who strive in His cause with their wealth and their lives. This is the covenant taken from the earlier and later generations alike, as He says, exalted is He:

“And when Allah took the covenant of the prophets: ‘Whatever I give you of Scripture and wisdom, should a messenger then come to you confirming what you have, you must believe in him and support him.’ He said, ‘Do you acknowledge this and accept My binding covenant?’ They said, ‘We acknowledge it.’ He said, ‘Then bear witness, and I too am among the witnesses with you.’”

Ibn ʿAbbās said: “Allah never sent a prophet without taking a covenant from him that, if Muhammad were sent while he was still alive, he would certainly believe in him and support him. He also commanded him to take a covenant from his people that, if Muhammad were sent while they were still alive, they would certainly believe in him and support him.”

He also says, exalted is He:

“We certainly sent Our messengers with clear proofs, and sent down with them the Scripture and the balance so that people might uphold justice. And We sent down iron, in which there is great might and benefits for people, and so that Allah may know who

supports Him and His messengers unseen. Indeed, Allah is All-Powerful, Almighty.”

He, exalted is He, thus states that He sent down the Scripture and the balance, and that He sent down iron, so that justice might be upheld and so that Allah may know who supports Him and His messengers. Thus, religion is sustained by a Scripture that guides and a sword that supports; and sufficient is your Lord as a Guide and Helper. Although both the Scripture and iron are described as having been sent down, this does not preclude their having been sent down from different sources.

The Scripture was sent down from Allah, as He, exalted is He, says:

“The revelation of the Scripture is from Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise.”

He also says:

“Alif Lām Rā. A Scripture whose verses have been perfected and then explained in detail, from One who is All-Wise, All-Aware.”

And He says:

“Indeed, you receive the Quran from One who is All-Wise, All-Knowing.”

Iron, by contrast, was sent down from the mountains in which it was created.

Likewise, He describes those who are truthful in their claim to righteousness—which encompasses the whole religion—in His words, exalted is He:

“Righteousness is not that you turn your faces toward the east or the west, but righteous is the one who believes in Allah, the Last Day, the angels, the Scripture, and the prophets.”

Up to His words:

“It is they who are truthful, and it is they who are mindful of Allah.”

As for the hypocrites, He, glorified is He, describes them as liars in numerous verses, such as His words, exalted is He:

“In their hearts is a disease, so Allah has increased their disease; and they will have a painful punishment because they used to lie.”

And His words:

“When the hypocrites come to you, they say, ‘We testify that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah.’ Allah knows that you are indeed His Messenger, and Allah testifies that the hypocrites are indeed liars.”

And His words:

“So He afflicted their hearts with hypocrisy until the Day they meet Him, because they broke the promise they had made to Allah and because they used to lie.”

There are many similar passages in the Quran. It should also be understood that truthfulness and affirmation are found both in words and in

deeds, as in the saying of the Prophet—may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace—in the authentic hadith:

“The son of Adam’s share of unlawful sexual intercourse has been decreed for him, and he will inevitably encounter it. The eyes commit it through looking, the ears through listening, the hands through grasping, and the feet through walking. The heart wishes and desires, and the private parts confirm this or deny it.”

People also say, “They made a true charge against the enemy,” when their resolve to fight is firm and unwavering. They say, “So-and-so is true in his love and affection,” and similar expressions. Thus, by a truthful person they mean someone true in his will, intention, and pursuit—someone true in his deeds. They also mean someone truthful in his reports and speech. The hypocrite is the opposite of the truthful believer: he is false either in what he says or in what he does, like someone who performs deeds to show off.

Allah, exalted is He, says:

“Indeed, the hypocrites seek to deceive Allah, but it is He who deceives them. When they rise for prayer, they rise lazily, showing off before people”—and so on through the following verse.

As for sincerity, it is the very essence of Islam, for Islam means submission to Allah, not to anyone else. As He, exalted is He, says:

“Allah presents an example: a man belonging to quarrelling partners, and a man belonging exclusively to one man—are the two equal?”—to the end of the verse.

Whoever does not submit to Allah has acted arrogantly, and whoever submits to Allah and to others has associated partners with Him. Both arrogance and associating partners with Allah are contrary to Islam, and Islam is contrary to both.

The corresponding verb is used both intransitively and transitively, as He, exalted is He, says:

“When his Lord said to him, ‘Submit,’ he said, ‘I have submitted to the Lord of all worlds.’”

And He, exalted is He, says:

“Yes indeed! Whoever submits his face to Allah while doing good will have his reward with his Lord. No fear will be upon them, nor will they grieve.”

There are many similar passages in the Quran.

For this reason, the foundation of Islam is “the testimony that none has the right to be worshipped but Allah.” This entails worshipping Allah alone and abandoning the worship of all else. This is Islam in its universal sense, besides which Allah accepts no religion from earlier or later generations. As He, exalted is He, says:

“Whoever seeks a religion other than Islam, it will never be accepted from him, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers.”

And He, exalted is He, says:

“Allah bears witness that there is no deity but Him, as do the angels and those endowed with knowledge. He upholds justice. There is no deity but Him, the Almighty, the All-Wise.”

“Indeed, the religion in the sight of Allah is Islam.”

What we have mentioned makes clear that the true foundation of religion consists of inward knowledge and deeds, and that outward deeds are of no benefit without them. As the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—said in the hadith narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad:

“Islam is outward, while faith is in the heart.”

For this reason, the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—said in the hadith reported by both al-Bukhārī and Muslim, on the authority of al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr, who narrated from the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“What is lawful is clear, and what is unlawful is clear. Between them are doubtful matters of which many people have no knowledge. Whoever avoids doubtful matters safeguards his honour and religion, while whoever falls into doubtful matters falls into the unlawful, like a shepherd grazing his flock around a protected pasture, on the verge of entering it. Indeed, every king has a protected domain, and Allah’s protected domain is what He has forbidden. Indeed, within the body is a morsel of flesh: when it is sound, the rest of the body is sound, and when it is corrupt, the rest of the body is corrupt. Indeed, it is the heart.”

Abū Hurayrah said: “The heart is a king, and the limbs are its soldiers. When the king is good, its soldiers are good; when the king is corrupt, its soldiers are corrupt.”

These inward deeds—such as loving Allah, being sincere to Him, relying upon Him, being content with Him, and the like—are all commanded of the elite and ordinary believers alike. Abandoning them is never praiseworthy for anyone, however elevated their spiritual station may be.

As for “sorrow,” neither Allah nor His Messenger has commanded it. Rather, Allah has forbidden it in several places, even when it concerns religious matters, as in His words, exalted is He:

“Do not lose heart or grieve, for you will have the upper hand, if you are believers.”

And His words:

“Do not grieve over them, nor be distressed by what they plot.”

And His words:

“When he said to his companion, ‘Do not grieve; Allah is with us.’”

And His words:

“Do not let their words grieve you.”

And His words:

“So that you may not grieve over what you have missed, nor exult in what He has given you.”

There are many similar passages. This is because sorrow neither brings benefit nor wards off harm, and thus serves no useful purpose. Allah does not command what serves no useful purpose. Nevertheless, a person incurs no sin on account of sorrow so long as it is not accompanied by anything forbidden, as when someone grieves over calamities. “He turned away from them and said, ‘Alas for Joseph!’ His eyes turned white with grief, and he held back his sorrow.”

Sorrow may be accompanied by something for which a person is rewarded and praised. It is then praiseworthy in that respect, not on account of the sorrow itself. For example, someone may grieve over a calamity affecting his religion or over calamities befalling Muslims generally. Such a person is rewarded for the love of good and hatred of evil in his heart, and for what follows from these. However, if sorrow over such matters leads to neglecting something commanded—such as patience, striving, securing a benefit, or warding off harm—it is forbidden. Otherwise, it is enough for the person that he bears no sin on account of the sorrow itself. But if it weakens his heart and so preoccupies it that he fails to do what Allah and His Messenger have commanded, he is blameworthy in that respect, even if he is praiseworthy in another.

As for loving Allah, relying upon Him, being sincere to Him, and the like, these are all pure good. They are virtuous and beloved in the case of everyone: the prophets, the steadfastly truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous. Whoever says that these spiritual stations belong to ordinary believers rather than the elite is mistaken if he means that the elite pass beyond them. No believer ever passes beyond them; only a disbeliever or a hypocrite departs from them. Some have made statements on this subject whose error we have explained at length, showing that they reflect a failure to realize these stations fully. This is not the place for that discussion.

However, people differ in these “spiritual stations,” some belonging to the elite and others to ordinary believers. The elite have their distinctive forms of these stations, while ordinary believers have their general forms. For example, these people say:

“You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help.”

, the Most Merciful.’ Allah says, ‘My servant has extolled Me.’ The servant says, ‘Master of the Day of Judgment.’ Allah says, ‘My servant has glorified Me.’ The servant says, ‘You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help.’ Allah says, ‘This verse is divided into two halves between Myself and My servant, and My servant shall have what he asks for.’ The servant says, ‘Guide us to the straight path—the path of those You have blessed, not those who have incurred Your anger, nor those who have gone astray.’ Allah says, ‘These are for My servant, and My servant shall have what he asks for.’”

Thus, the half consisting of praise and goodness belongs to the Lord, glorified is He, while the half consisting of supplication and petition belongs to the servant. These two statements encompass what belongs to the Lord, glorified is He, and what belongs to the servant: “You alone we worship” is for the Lord, and “You alone we ask for help” is for the servant.

In the two Sahīh collections, Mu‘ādh, may Allah be pleased with him, reported:

“I was riding behind the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on a donkey. He said, ‘O Mu‘ādh, do you know Allah’s right over His servants?’

“I said, ‘Allah and His Messenger know best.’

“He said, ‘Allah’s right over His servants is that they worship Him and associate nothing with Him. Do you know the servants’ right upon Allah if they do that?’

“I said, ‘Allah and His Messenger know best.’

“He said, ‘Their right upon Him is that He not punish them.’”

Worship is the purpose for which Allah created His servants, in respect of what He commands, loves, and is pleased with. As He, exalted is He, says:

“I did not create jinn and mankind except to worship Me.”

It was with this that He sent the messengers and revealed the scriptures. Worship is a term encompassing the fullest and utmost love for Allah together with the fullest and utmost humility before Him. Love devoid of humility, and humility devoid of love, do not constitute worship. Rather, worship combines both in their fullest measure. For this reason, worship is fitting for Allah alone. Although its benefit accrues to the servant, while Allah has no need of any of creation, it is for Him in that He loves it and is pleased with it. For this reason, Allah rejoices more at His servant’s repentance than

a man who has lost his mount, carrying his food and drink, in a deadly wilderness, falls asleep having despaired of recovering it, then awakens to find it. Allah rejoices more at His servant’s repentance than this man rejoices at recovering his mount. This concerns matters of great importance, which we have discussed and explained at length elsewhere.

Reliance upon Allah and seeking His help are for the servant, for they are the means and the path by which he attains his aim and what he seeks through worship. Seeking help is thus like supplication and petition. Al-Tabarānī related in his Book of Supplication that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ‘O son of Adam, there are but four matters: one for Me, one for you, one between Me and you, and one between you and My creation. As for the one for Me, it is that you worship Me, associating nothing with Me. As for the one for you, it is your deeds, for which I shall recompense you when you are most in need of that recompense. As for the one between Me and you, yours is to supplicate and Mine is to answer. As for the one between you and My creation, treat people as you would like them to treat you.’”

Describing one as being for Allah and the other as being for the servant concerns what love and pleasure are directed toward in the first instance. The servant initially loves and desires what he considers beneficial to himself, whereas Allah, exalted is He, loves and is pleased with what constitutes the ultimate object of His pleasure, and loves the means as subordinate to that. Both, however, are commanded; their benefit accrues to the servant, and Allah loves and is pleased with all of this.

Accordingly, whoever considered reliance upon Allah to be one of the general spiritual stations assumed that it is sought only for worldly benefits. This is mistaken; rather, reliance upon Allah in religious matters is greater.

translated_text:
Moreover, reliance upon Allah is among the religious practices without which obligatory and recommended deeds cannot be fully accomplished. Whoever renounces these practices renounces what Allah loves, commands, and is pleased with.

“Religiously prescribed renunciation” means relinquishing desire for what brings no benefit in the Hereafter: superfluous lawful things that do not help one obey Allah. Likewise, “religiously prescribed scrupulousness” means abandoning what may cause harm in the Hereafter: abandoning forbidden and doubtful matters, where doing so does not entail neglecting something whose performance takes precedence, such as obligatory duties. As for what benefits one in the Hereafter in itself, or helps one attain such benefit, renouncing it is no part of religion. Rather, whoever does so falls within the scope of the words of Allah, exalted is He:

“O you who believe, do not forbid the good things Allah has made lawful for you, and do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not love transgressors.”

Likewise, occupying oneself with superfluous lawful things is the opposite of religiously prescribed renunciation. If these things distract someone from performing an obligation or [refraining from] (1) something forbidden, he is sinning. Otherwise, he falls short of the rank of those brought near to Allah, descending to the rank of those who take a middle course.

Furthermore, reliance upon Allah is beloved to Allah, pleasing to Him, and commanded at all times. Whatever Allah loves, is pleased with, and commands at all times cannot be a practice of those who take a middle course to the exclusion of those brought near to Him. These, then, are three responses to their assertion: “The person who relies upon Allah seeks his own benefits.”

As for their assertion that all matters have already been settled, this resembles what some of them have said about supplication: that there is no need for it, because if what is sought has been decreed, there is no need for supplication, and if it has not been

translated_text:
decreed, supplication will be of no avail. This is among the most unsound views, both in terms of religious teaching and reason.

Equally unsound is the assertion:

“Reliance upon Allah and supplication neither bring benefit nor avert harm; they are merely acts of worship. The true nature of reliance upon Allah is equivalent to simply entrusting all matters to Him.”

Although some shaykhs have said this, it too is mistaken. The same applies to the assertion that supplication is merely an act of worship.

These views and others like them share a single underlying premise: their proponents imagined that, because matters are already ordained and decreed, they cannot depend upon causes that are likewise ordained and that involve the servant’s actions. They failed to understand that Allah, glorified is He, ordains and decrees matters through the causes upon which He has made them dependent, whether those causes are people’s actions or otherwise. Thus, pursuing their argument to its logical conclusion would entail abandoning action altogether.

The Prophet—may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace—was asked about this principle on several occasions and answered it. Thus, both compilers relate in their Sahīh collections that ʿImrān ibn Husayn said:

“The Messenger of Allah—may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace—was asked, ‘O Messenger of Allah, are those destined for Paradise and those destined for Hell already known?’

“He replied, ‘Yes.’

“They asked, ‘Then what is the purpose of deeds?’

“He replied, ‘Everyone is enabled to do that for which he was created.’”

Also in the two Sahīh collections, ʿAlī ibn Abī Tālib said:

“We were attending a funeral at which the Messenger of Allah—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—was present. He sat down with a walking stick and began poking the ground with it. Then he raised his head and said, ‘There is no soul born whose place in Hell or Paradise has not already been written down, and who has not already been recorded as wretched or blessed.’” He continued:

“Then a man among those present said, ‘O Prophet of Allah, should we not simply rely on what has been written for us and abandon deeds? Whoever is destined for blessedness will surely attain blessedness, and whoever is destined for wretchedness will surely come to wretchedness.’

He replied, ‘Act, for everyone is enabled to do that for which he was created. Those destined for blessedness are enabled to attain blessedness, and those destined for wretchedness are enabled to attain wretchedness.’ Then the Prophet of Allah—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—recited:

‘As for the one who gives and fears Allah,
and believes in the best reward,
We will make easy for him the way of ease.
But as for the one who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient,
and denies the best reward,
We will make easy for him the way of hardship.’”

This was related by the hadith compilers in their Sahīh, Sunan, and Musnad collections. Al-Tirmidhī also related:

“The Prophet—may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace—was asked, ‘O Messenger of Allah, what of the medicines we use, the healing recitations we ask others to perform for us, and the precautions we take? Do they avert anything of Allah’s decree?’

He replied, ‘They are part of Allah’s decree.’”

This meaning has been conveyed from the Prophet—may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace—in several hadiths. He—may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace—thus explained that Allah’s prior knowledge and recording of who is blessed and who is wretched do not preclude the former’s attaining blessedness through righteous deeds and the latter’s becoming wretched through evil deeds. For He, glorified is He, knows things as they are and records them accordingly. He knows that the blessed attain blessedness through righteous deeds and that the wretched become wretched through evil deeds. Thus, whoever is blessed is enabled to perform the righteous deeds that lead to blessedness, and whoever is wretched is enabled to perform evil deeds

translated_text:
that lead to wretchedness; each is enabled to do that for which he was created, namely, the outcome he reaches in accordance with Allah’s all-encompassing will governing creation. Allah, glorified is He, mentions this in His Book, saying:

“They will continue to differ, except those upon whom your Lord has mercy—and for this He created them.”

As for the purpose of their creation that Allah loves and approves—corresponding to His religious will, in accordance with which they have been commanded—it is mentioned in His words:

“I did not create jinn and mankind except to worship Me.”

Allah, glorified is He, has clarified in His Book, with respect to each of the terms “words,” “command,” “will,” “permission,” “writing,” “judgment,” “decree,” “prohibition,” and similar expressions, what pertains to religion and accords with His love, approval, and legislative command, and what pertains to creation and accords with His will governing creation.

For example, concerning His command in matters of religion, He says:

“Indeed, Allah commands justice, good conduct, and giving to relatives.”

And He, exalted is He, says:

“Indeed, Allah commands you to return trusts to their rightful owners.”

There are other similar passages. Concerning His command governing creation, He says:

“When He wills a thing, His command is only to say to it, ‘Be,’ and it is.”

Likewise, He says:

“When We intend to destroy a town, We command its affluent, and they transgress within it, so the sentence against it becomes binding.”

This is according to one of the interpretations of this verse. Concerning His religious will, He says:

“Allah intends ease for you and does not intend hardship for you.”

“Allah intends to make things clear to you, guide you to the ways of those before you, and accept your repentance. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.”

“Allah does not intend to place any hardship upon you, but He intends to purify you.”

Concerning His will governing creation, He says:

“If Allah had willed, they would not have fought one another, but Allah does what He wills.”

And He says:

“Whoever Allah wills to guide, He opens his heart to Islam; and whoever He wills to lead astray, He makes his heart tight and constricted, as though he were climbing into the sky.”

Noah, peace be upon him, said:

“My advice will not benefit you, even if I wish to advise you, if Allah wills to lead you astray.”

And He, exalted is He, says:

“When He wills a thing, His command is only to say to it, ‘Be,’ and it is.”

Concerning His permission in matters of religion, He, exalted is He, says:

“Whatever palm trees you cut down or left standing on their roots, it was by Allah’s permission, so that He might disgrace the defiantly disobedient.”

Concerning His permission governing creation, He, exalted is He, says:

“They cannot harm anyone through it except by Allah’s permission.”

Concerning His decree in matters of religion, He, exalted is He, says:

“Your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him.”

That is, He has commanded it. Concerning His decree governing creation, He, exalted is He, says:

“He formed them into seven heavens in two days.”

Concerning His judgment in matters of religion, He, exalted is He, says:

“Livestock have been made lawful for you, except what is recited to you, but hunting is not lawful while you are in a state of consecration for pilgrimage. Indeed, Allah rules as He wills.”

And He, exalted is He, says:

“That is Allah’s judgment; He judges between you.”

Concerning His judgment governing creation, He, exalted is He, relates the words of Jacob’s son:

“I will never leave this land until my father gives me permission or Allah judges in my favor, and He is the best of judges.”

And He, exalted is He, says:

“He said, ‘My Lord, judge in truth. Our Lord is the Most Merciful, whose help is sought against what you allege.’”

Concerning His prohibition in matters of religion, He, exalted is He, says:

“Forbidden to you are carrion, blood, and the flesh of swine.”

“Forbidden to you are your mothers and your daughters”—to the end of the verse.

Concerning His prohibition governing creation, He, exalted is He, says:

“It is forbidden to them for forty years, during which they will wander through the land.”

And He, exalted is He, says:

“And those in whose wealth there is a recognized right for the beggar and the deprived.”

Concerning His words in matters of religion, He, exalted is He, says:

“And when Abraham’s Lord tested him with commands, which he fulfilled.”

Concerning His words governing creation, He, exalted is He, says:

“And your Lord’s gracious word to the Children of Israel was fulfilled because of their patience.”

Another example is the saying of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, widely transmitted from him through numerous chains in the collections of authentic hadith, Sunan, and Musnads. When seeking refuge, he would say:

“I seek refuge in Allah’s perfect words, beyond which neither the righteous nor the wicked can pass.”

It is well known that these are His words governing creation: nothing falls outside His will and His act of creation. As for His words in matters of religion, the wicked have contravened them by disobeying Him.

The point here is that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, explained that the way is made easy for people to reach the final destinies of happiness or misery for which they were created, through the deeds that lead them there. The same applies to all other created things. He, glorified is He, creates children and other living creatures in wombs through His ordaining the mating of the two parents and the meeting of their two fluids in the womb. Thus, if someone were to say, “I put my trust in Allah and will not have intercourse with my wife, for if it has already been

decreed that I should have a child, it will come into being; otherwise it will not, and there is no need for intercourse,” he would be a fool. This is unlike someone who has intercourse but withdraws before ejaculation, for withdrawal does not prevent a child from being conceived if Allah wills, since semen may escape involuntarily. An example of this is the report established in the two Sahīh collections from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, who said:

“We went out with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on the campaign against Banū al-Mustaliq and took some Arab captives. We desired women, found abstinence very difficult, and wished to practise withdrawal. We asked the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, about this, and he said, ‘There is no harm in your not doing so, for Allah has already decreed whatever He will create until the Day of Resurrection.’”

In Sahīh Muslim, Jābir reported:

“A man came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said, ‘I have a slave woman who serves us and waters our date palms. I have intercourse with her, but I do not want her to become pregnant.’ He said, ‘Practise withdrawal with her if you wish, for whatever has been decreed for her will come to her.’”

All this is so even though Allah, glorified is He, is capable of what He has already done: creating a human being without either parent, as He created Adam; creating someone from a father alone, as He created Eve from Adam’s short rib; and creating someone from a mother alone, as He created the Messiah, son of Mary, peace be upon him. But He brought these creations into being through other, unusual causes.

Although this matter is denied only by heretics who set aside the revealed laws, many revered shaykhs have fallen into error over many of its subtleties: one of them lets himself drift along with the divine decree

without duly upholding His commands and prohibitions, regarding this as entrusting his affairs to Allah, relying upon Him, and going along with the reality of divine decree. He imagines that the saying, “The servant should be with Allah like a corpse in the hands of the one washing it,” entails ceasing to observe commands and prohibitions. Thus he abandons what he has been commanded to do and does what he has been forbidden, until the light and discernment by which he distinguishes between what Allah has commanded, loved, and approved, and what He has forbidden, hated, and been displeased with, grow dim within him. He then treats as equal what Allah has distinguished, as the Most High says:

“Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will make them like those who believe and do righteous deeds, equal in their life and their death? Evil is their judgment!”

The Most High also says:

“Shall We then treat those who submit to Allah like the criminals? What is the matter with you? How do you judge?”

And the Most High says:

“Shall We treat those who believe and do righteous deeds like those who spread corruption on earth? Or shall We treat the righteous like the wicked?”

And the Most High says:

“Say: Are those who know equal to those who do not know?”

And the Most High says:

“The blind and the seeing are not equal,”

“nor are darkness and light,”

“nor shade and scorching heat,”

“nor are the living and the dead equal. Indeed, Allah causes whom He wills to hear, but you cannot make those in the graves hear.”

There are many similar passages. Matters go so far with the extremists among them that they no longer distinguish between the command to carry out what Allah and His Prophet have prescribed in the revealed law, which distinguishes truth from falsehood—as set out in the Quran and Sunnah—and the states that occur in existence through unbelievers and the wicked. They perceive what unites all these things in that they all come about through Allah’s decree, predestination, lordship, and universal will

and that all of it falls within His dominion. Yet they fail to perceive the distinction Allah has drawn between His allies and His enemies, the righteous and the wicked, believers and unbelievers, and the obedient who heed His religious command and the disobedient who defy it. To support this, they cite ambiguous statements transmitted from certain spiritual masters, or some of those masters’ errors.

This is a “momentous principle,” among the matters most deserving of attention from those who tread the path to Allah and follow the way of aspiration—the aspiration of those who seek His Face. Through neglecting it, some groups among them have fallen into unbelief, wickedness, and disobedience to an extent known only to Allah. They even become accomplices in oppression and aggression to unjust and arrogant men who wield power on earth. Such are those who direct their hearts toward assisting those they favor among the people who seek supremacy and spread corruption on earth, imagining that if they possess inward states through which they exert an influence in this regard, they are thereby among Allah’s allies.

For hearts exert a greater influence than bodies. If they are sound, their influence is sound; if they are corrupt, their influence is corrupt. Thus, the influence of these states is sometimes beloved to Allah and sometimes hateful to Him. The jurists have discussed the obligation to exact retribution by execution from someone who kills another by inward means, where such retribution is warranted.

In their inner selves and hearts, they appeal to the universal decree as evidence. They regard the mere occurrence of something beyond the ordinary for one of them—whether an unveiling granted to him or an influence that accords with his will—as an honor bestowed upon him by Allah. They do not realize that it is, in reality, a humiliation, that true honor lies in steadfast uprightness, and that

Allah has bestowed no greater honor upon His servant than conformity to what He loves and is pleased with: obedience to Him and His Messenger, allegiance to His allies, and enmity toward His enemies. These are the allies of Allah of whom He says:

“Unquestionably, the allies of Allah will have no fear, nor will they grieve.”

If they conform to what He has made obligatory upon them, they are among those who follow the middle course. If they conform both to what He has made obligatory and to what He loves, they are among those brought near to Him—although everything obligatory is beloved to Him, not everything beloved to Him is obligatory.

As for the ease with which Allah tests His servant, whether through extraordinary occurrences or otherwise, or the adversity with which He tests him, this is not because the servant is honored or despised by his Lord. Rather, some may attain felicity through these trials if they obey Him in them, while others may come to misery through them if they disobey Him in them.

Allah Most High says:

“As for man, when his Lord tests him by honoring him and granting him blessings, he says, ‘My Lord has honored me.’

“But when He tests him by restricting his provision, he says, ‘My Lord has humiliated me.’ No!”

Thus, with regard to these matters, people fall into “three categories”:

Those whose ranks are raised through extraordinary occurrences when they use them in obedience to Allah; those who expose themselves to Allah’s punishment when they use them in disobedience to Allah, such as Balaam and others; and those for whom they have the status of permissible things.

The first category consists of the true believers who follow their Prophet, the foremost of Adam’s descendants. His extraordinary occurrences served only to provide proof by which he established Allah’s religion, or to meet a need that helped him obey Allah.

Because errors concerning this principle are so widespread, the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) forbade passively yielding to divine decree without striving to do what one has been commanded and what benefits one. Muslim narrated in his Sahīh from Abū Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said:

“The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, though there is good in both. Strive for what benefits you, seek Allah’s help, and do not give in to helplessness. If something befalls you, do not say, ‘If only I had done such and such, this and that would have happened.’ Rather, say, ‘Allah decreed this and did as He willed,’ for ‘if only’ opens the door to Satan’s work.”

In Sunan Abī Dāwūd, it is related:

“Two men brought a dispute before the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), and he ruled against one of them. The man against whom he ruled said, ‘Allah is sufficient for me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.’ The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said, ‘Allah censures helpless inaction. Rather, you must be resourceful; then, if something overcomes you, say: Allah is sufficient for me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.’”

Thus, the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) commanded the believer to strive for what benefits him and to seek Allah’s help. This accords with the words of the Most High:

“You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help,”

and His words:

“So worship Him and put your trust in Him.”

Striving for what benefits the servant means obeying and worshipping Allah, for obedience to Allah is what benefits him, and nothing benefits him more. Everything that helps one obey Allah is itself an act of obedience, even if it belongs to the category of permissible things.

The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said to Saʿd in an authentic hadith:

“You will never

spend anything seeking Allah’s countenance without thereby rising in rank and standing—even the morsel you place in your wife’s mouth.”

The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) thus explained that Allah censures helpless inaction, which is the opposite of resourcefulness: neglecting what one is commanded to do. Such neglect is incompatible with the capacity that accompanies an act, although it is not incompatible with the prior capacity upon which commands and prohibitions are predicated. For the capacity that necessarily entails an act accompanies it and pertains only to the act it enables, as Allah Most High mentions in His words:

“They were unable to hear,”

and His words:

“And they were unable to hear.”

As for the capacity to which commands and prohibitions relate, it may or may not be accompanied by the act. Thus Allah Most High says:

“Pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed to Allah by those who are able to make their way there.”

And the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said to ʿImrān ibn Husayn:

“Pray standing; if you cannot, then sitting; and if you cannot, then on your side.”

On this matter, people fall into “four categories.” Some attend to commands and prohibitions, worship and obedience, acknowledging the divinity of the Lord—glory be to Him—whom they have been commanded to worship. Yet they do not attend to divine decree and predestination, trust in Allah, and seeking His help. This is the condition of many who engage in religious learning and devotional practice. Despite their good intentions and their reverence for Allah’s sacred bounds and rites, they are often overcome by weakness, helplessness, and lack of support. For it is seeking Allah’s help, trusting in Him, taking refuge in Him, and supplicating to Him that strengthen the servant and make his affairs easier.

For this reason, one of the early generations said:

“Whoever wishes to be the strongest of people should put his trust in Allah.”

In the two Sahīh collections, ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr reports that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) is described in the Torah as follows:

“We have sent you as a witness, a bearer of glad tidings, a warner, and a safeguard for the unlettered. You are My servant and My messenger; I have named you ‘the one who trusts in Allah.’ He is neither harsh nor hard-hearted, nor does he raise his voice in the marketplaces. He does not repay evil with evil; rather, he repays evil with good, pardoning and forgiving. I will not take his soul until, through him, I have set the crooked religion straight and opened blind eyes, deaf ears, and closed hearts, through their saying: ‘There is no god but Allah.’”

For this reason, it is reported that the bearers of the Throne were only able to bear it by saying, “There is no might nor power except through Allah.” It is established in the two Sahīh collections that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said:

“These words are one of the treasures of Paradise.”

Allah Most High says:

“Whoever puts his trust in Allah, He will suffice him.”

And He Most High says:

“Those to whom people said, ‘The people have gathered against you, so fear them,’ but this only increased them in faith, and they said, ‘Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best disposer of affairs.’”

Through to His words:

“So do not fear them, but fear Me, if you are believers.”

In Sahīh al-Bukhārī, Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with him), commenting on the words, “And they said, ‘Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best disposer of affairs,’” said: “Abraham, Allah’s close friend, said these words when he was cast into the fire, and Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him) said them when people told them, ‘The people have gathered against you.’”

base their actions on spiritual states through which they exert influence in the world, without seeking what pleases the Lord and what He loves. They frequently err, imagining that disobeying Him is what pleases Him. They thus end up setting aside His commands and prohibitions, calling this “reality.” They imagine that they must follow this reality of divine decree without restraint, disregarding the religious reality of His commands, which encompasses what pleases the Lord, what He loves, and His commands and prohibitions, both outwardly and inwardly.

Such people are often deprived of their spiritual states and may revert to various forms of sin and wickedness. Indeed, many of them turn away from Islam altogether, for the good outcome belongs to those who fear Allah. Whoever does not observe the limits of Allah’s commands and prohibitions is not among the God-fearing. Thus, they fall into some of the same errors as the polytheists: sometimes adopting an innovation they imagine to be divinely prescribed, and sometimes invoking divine decree against His commands.

When Allah Most High mentioned the things for which He condemned the polytheists in Surahs al-An'ām and al-A'rāf, He mentioned the religious practices they had invented and made into prescribed law. As He Most High says:

“When they commit an indecency, they say, ‘We found our forefathers doing this, and Allah has commanded us to do it.’ Say, ‘Allah does not command indecency.’”

He condemned them for forbidding what Allah had not forbidden and prescribing what Allah had not prescribed. He also mentioned their appeal to divine decree in His words, Most High:

“Those who associated others with Allah said, ‘Had Allah willed, neither we nor our forefathers would have worshipped anything besides Him, nor would we have forbidden anything without His command.’”

Similar passages occur in Surahs al-Nahl, Yā Sīn, and al-Zukhruf. These people bear a resemblance to the polytheists in both respects.

As for the third category—those who turn away from worshipping Allah and seeking His help—they are the worst of these categories.

The fourth category is the praiseworthy one: those who have truly fulfilled the words:

“You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help,”

and His words:

“So worship Him and put your trust in Him.”

They sought His help in obeying Him and acknowledged that He is their God, whom alone they may worship, through obedience to Him and His Messenger. They acknowledged that He is their Lord:

“They have no protector or intercessor besides Him.”

They also acknowledged the truths expressed in His words:

“Whatever mercy Allah grants to people, none can withhold; and whatever He withholds, none can release thereafter.”

“If Allah touches you with harm, none can remove it except Him; and if He intends good for you, none can repel His bounty.”

“Say, ‘Have you considered those you invoke besides Allah? If Allah intended harm for me, could they remove His harm? Or if He intended mercy for me, could they withhold His mercy?’”

For this reason, a number of scholars have said: “Turning to causes constitutes associating partners with Allah, contrary to His oneness; denying that causes are causes is a deficiency in reason; and disregarding causes altogether undermines the revealed law.” The trust in Allah that is commanded brings together the requirements of monotheism, reason, and the revealed law.

It has thus become clear that anyone who considers trust in Allah to be one of the spiritual stations of ordinary followers of the path has made a grave error, even if he is a leading shaykh—such as the author of ‘Ilal al-Maqāmāt (The Defects of the Spiritual Stations), who is among the most eminent shaykhs, and from whom the author of Mahāsin al-Majālis (The Merits of Gatherings) adopted this view.

The weakness of the argument advanced by those who hold this view has also become clear: they suppose that trust in Allah serves only the interests of ordinary people and contributes nothing to attaining the intended goal. The same applies to those who regard supplication in this way. This is akin to regarding the commanded deeds in the same way—as in the case of someone whose preoccupation with trusting in Allah distracts him from what is required of him in the way of

taking the means that constitute prescribed acts of worship and obedience. If this person errs by abandoning the prescribed means included in Allah’s words,

“So worship Him and put your trust in Him,”

his error resembles that of the former person in abandoning the prescribed trust in Allah included in His words,

“So worship Him and put your trust in Him.”

However, it should be said: whoever trusts in Allah and supplicates to Him to obtain permissible things is among ordinary people; if he does so to accomplish recommended and obligatory deeds, he is among the elect. Likewise, whoever supplicates to Him and trusts in Him to obtain forbidden things wrongs himself. Whoever turns away from trusting in Allah disobeys Allah and His Messenger; indeed, he falls outside the reality of faith. How, then, can this station belong to the elect? Allah Most High says:

“Moses said, ‘O my people, if you have believed in Allah, then put your trust in Him, if you are Muslims.’”

He Most High also says:

“If Allah helps you, none can overcome you; but if He forsakes you, who can help you after Him?”

And He Most High says:

“And in Allah let the believers put their trust.”

He Most High also says:

“Say, ‘Have you considered those you invoke besides Allah? If Allah intended harm for me, could they remove His harm?’”

Further on, He says:

“Say, ‘Allah is sufficient for me. In Him those who trust should put their trust.’”

Allah has mentioned these words, “Allah is sufficient for me,” sometimes in connection with obtaining benefit and at other times with averting harm. The first occurs in His words:

“If only they had been content with what Allah and His Messenger gave them and had said, ‘Allah is sufficient for us. Allah will give us from His bounty, and so will His Messenger,’”

to the end of the verse.

The second occurs in His words:

“Those to whom people said, ‘The people have gathered against you

, so fear them.’ But this only increased them in faith, and they said, ‘Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.’” And in His words, Most High:

“But if they intend to deceive you, then Allah is sufficient for you. He is the One who strengthened you with His help.”

His words,

“If only they had been content with what Allah and His Messenger gave them and had said, ‘Allah is sufficient for us. Allah will give us from His bounty, and so will His Messenger,’”

contain a command to be content and to put one’s trust in Allah. Contentment and trust in Allah stand on either side of what has been decreed: trust precedes its occurrence, while contentment follows it. Thus, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would say in prayer:

“O Allah, by Your knowledge of the unseen and Your power over creation, keep me alive so long as life is better for me, and cause me to die when death is better for me. O Allah, I ask You to grant me fear of You in private and in public. I ask You to enable me to speak the truth in anger and in contentment. I ask You for moderation in poverty and in wealth. I ask You for bliss that never ends, and joy that never ceases. O Allah, I ask You for contentment after Your decree, and I ask You for the comfort of life after death. I ask You for the delight of looking upon Your Face, and I ask You for longing to meet You, without harmful adversity or a trial that leads astray. O Allah, adorn us with the adornment of faith, and make us rightly guided guides.”

This was narrated by Ahmad and al-Nasā’ī from the hadith of ‘Ammār ibn Yāsir.

What exists before the decree, however, is a resolve to be content, not actual contentment. Thus, some spiritual masters would resolve to be content before affliction struck, but when it did, their resolve crumbled. Something similar happens with patience and other qualities, as Allah Most High says:

“You certainly wished for death before you encountered it. Now you have seen it with your own eyes.”

And He Most High says:

“O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do?”

“It is greatly hateful to Allah that you say what you do not do.”

“Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in ranks as though they were a building

firmly joined together.”

This verse was revealed when they said, “If we knew which deeds were most beloved to Allah, we would perform them.” Allah, Glorified and Most High, then revealed the verse concerning fighting in His cause, and some were averse to it.

For this reason, it is disliked for a person to expose himself to trials by binding himself, through pledges, vows, or the like, to something the Lawgiver has not made obligatory upon him; by seeking a position of authority; or by entering a land where there is plague. Thus, it is established through several routes in the two Sahīh collections that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, forbade making vows and said:

“It brings no good; it merely extracts something from the miser.”

It is also established in the two Sahīh collections that he said to ‘Abd al-Rahmān ibn Samura:

“Do not ask for authority. If you are given it because you asked, you will be left to bear it on your own; but if you are given it without asking, you will be helped in discharging it. If you swear an oath and then see that another course is better, do what is better and expiate your oath.”

It is also established in the two Sahīh collections that he said concerning plague:

“If you hear of it in a land, do not enter it. If it breaks out in a land while you are there, do not leave to flee from it.”

It is also established in the two Sahīh collections that he said:

“Do not wish to meet the enemy, and ask Allah for well-being. But when you do meet them, remain steadfast, and know that Paradise lies beneath the shade of swords.”

These and similar teachings indicate that a person should not pursue what imposes certain obligations and prohibitions upon him, only to become reluctant to fulfil his commitments—as happens with many who make covenants with Allah concerning various matters. Most such people fall into the trial of breaking their covenants.

They also indicate that when a person is tested, he must be patient and steadfast, and must not become complacent, so that he may be among those men who possess certainty and fulfil their obligations. All of this necessarily requires

patience. Hence, Muslims agree that patience is obligatory in fulfilling duties and avoiding prohibitions. This includes enduring afflictions without giving way to anguish, and restraining oneself from following personal desires in matters Allah has forbidden.

Allah mentions patience in His Book in more than ninety places, and links it with prayer in His words, Most High:

“Seek help through patience and prayer. Indeed, it is difficult except for the humbly submissive.”

“Seek help through patience and prayer. Indeed, Allah is with the patient.”

And His words:

“Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and in the early hours of the night,”

through to His words:

“And be patient, for Allah does not allow the reward of those who do good to be lost.”

“So be patient with what they say, and glorify your Lord with praise before sunrise and before sunset.”

“So be patient. Indeed, Allah’s promise is true. And seek forgiveness for your sin”—to the end of the verse.

He has made “leadership in religion” the fruit of patience and certainty, saying:

“And We made from among them leaders guiding by Our command when they were patient and were certain of Our signs.”

The whole of religion consists of knowing the truth and acting upon it. Acting upon it necessarily requires patience; indeed, even seeking knowledge of it requires patience. As Mu‘ādh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him, said:

“Devote yourselves to knowledge, for seeking it for Allah’s sake is worship; knowing it is reverent fear; researching it is striving in Allah’s cause; teaching it to those who do not know it is charity; and discussing it is glorification of Allah. Through it Allah is known and worshipped, and through it Allah is exalted and His oneness affirmed. Through knowledge Allah raises people, making them leaders and guides whom others follow and to whose judgment they defer.”

He thus regarded researching knowledge as a form of striving in Allah’s cause, and such striving necessarily requires patience. For this reason,

Allah Most High says:

“By time,
indeed, mankind is in loss,
except those who believe, do righteous deeds, urge one another to the truth, and urge one another to patience.”

And He says:

“Remember Our servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, men of strength and insight.”

Beneficial knowledge is the foundation of guidance, while acting upon the truth is right conduct. The opposite of the former is misguidance, and the opposite of the latter is waywardness. Misguidance is acting without knowledge, while waywardness is following one’s desires.

Allah Most High says:

“By the star when it descends,
your companion has neither strayed nor erred.”

Guidance can therefore be attained only through knowledge, and right conduct only through patience. For this reason, ‘Alī said:

“Indeed, patience is to faith what the head is to the body—when the head is cut off, the body is left without it.” Then he raised his voice and said: “Indeed, whoever has no patience has no faith.”

As for “contentment,” the scholars and spiritual masters among the followers of Imam Ahmad and others have differed over whether contentment with the divine decree is obligatory or recommended. There are two views: according to the first, it is among the deeds of those who take a middle course; according to the second, it is among the deeds of those brought near to Allah. ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-‘Azīz said: “Contentment is rare, but patience is the believer’s mainstay.”

It has been related that the Prophet, may Allah’s blessings and peace be upon him, said to Ibn ‘Abbās:

“If you can act for Allah’s sake with contentment and certainty, then do so. But if you cannot, there is much good in patiently enduring what you dislike.”

For this reason, the Quran praises those who are content, but does not make such contentment obligatory. This concerns contentment with the afflictions the Lord brings upon His servant, such as illness, poverty, and upheaval. Allah Most High says:

“Those who are patient in hardship and suffering, and in times of battle.”

And He says:

“Or do you think you will enter Paradise without experiencing the like of what befell those who passed away before you? Hardship and suffering afflicted them, and they were shaken.”

Hardship affects wealth, suffering affects the body, and upheaval affects the heart.

As for “contentment with what Allah has commanded,” its essential foundation is obligatory and is part of faith. As the Prophet, may Allah’s blessings and peace be upon him, said in an authentic hadith:

“He has tasted the sweetness of faith who is content with Allah as his Lord, Islam as his religion, and Muhammad as his Prophet.”

It is also a consequence of love, as we shall explain, if Allah Most High wills. Allah Most High says:

“But no, by your Lord, they will not believe until they make you judge over their disputes, then find within themselves no objection to your judgment and submit wholeheartedly.”

And He says:

“If only they had been content with what Allah and His Messenger had given them and had said, ‘Allah is sufficient for us’”—to the end of the verse.

And He says:

“That is because they followed what angered Allah and disliked His good pleasure, so He rendered their deeds worthless.”

And He says:

“Nothing prevents their contributions from being accepted except that they disbelieve in Allah and His Messenger, come to prayer only reluctantly, and spend only unwillingly.”

An example of “the first type” is what Ahmad, al-Tirmidhī, and others narrated from Sa‘d, from the Prophet, may Allah’s blessings and peace be upon him, who said:

“Part of the happiness of the son of Adam is his seeking guidance

from Allah and his contentment with what Allah has allotted him. And part of the misery of the son of Adam is his failure to seek guidance from Allah and his discontent with what Allah allots him.”

As for “contentment with prohibited things”—disbelief, wickedness, and disobedience—most scholars say that contentment with them is not sanctioned, just as loving them is not sanctioned. For Allah, glorified is He, neither approves of them nor loves them, even though He has ordained and decreed them. As He, glorified is He, says:

“Allah does not love corruption.”

And He Most High says:

“He does not approve of disbelief for His servants.”

And He Most High says:

“He is with them when they plot by night to say what He does not approve of.”

Rather, He is displeased with them, as He Most High says:

“That is because they followed what angered Allah and disliked His good pleasure, so He rendered their deeds worthless.”

A group of scholars said that one should be content with them insofar as they are attributed to Allah as His creation, and displeased with them insofar as they are attributed to the servant as acts he performs and acquires. This view does not contradict the preceding one; rather, both rest upon a single principle. He, glorified is He, has only decreed things for a wise purpose. In view of that purpose, they are loved and approved of, although in themselves they may be disliked and disapproved of.

For a single thing may combine two qualities: it is loved on account of one and disliked on account of the other. As stated in the authentic hadith:

“I do not hesitate over anything I am to do as I hesitate over taking the soul of My believing servant. He dislikes death, and I dislike causing him distress, yet he must undergo it.”

We have explained the related matters elsewhere.

Although contentment is an action of the heart, it finds its fullest expression in praise. Indeed, some have explained praise in terms of contentment. Hence the Quran and Sunnah teach praising Allah in every circumstance, for this entails contentment with His decree.

The hadith states:

It is reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace,

“When a servant’s child is taken in death, Allah says to His angels, ‘Have you taken the soul of My servant’s child?’ They reply, ‘Yes.’ He says, ‘Have you taken his heart’s delight?’ They reply, ‘Yes.’ He says, ‘What did My servant say?’ They reply, ‘He praised You and affirmed that to Allah we belong and to Him we return.’ He says, ‘Build My servant a house in Paradise and name it the House of Praise.’”

Our Prophet Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is the bearer of the Banner of Praise. His community are those who constantly praise Allah in prosperity and adversity.

Praising Allah in adversity is prompted by two considerations:

The first is the servant’s knowledge that Allah, glorified is He, deserves this praise and is entitled to it in His own right. For He has made excellent everything He created and has perfected everything. He is the All-Knowing, the All-Wise, the All-Aware, the Most Merciful.

The second is his knowledge that Allah’s choice for His believing servant is better than the servant’s choice for himself. Muslim relates in his Sahīh, as do others, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Indeed, in that are signs for everyone steadfast in patience and grateful.”

 وَالْمُؤْمِنُ إذَا فَعَلَ سَيِّئَةً فَإِنَّ عُقُوبَتَهَا تَنْدَفِعُ عَنْهُ بِعَشَرَةِ أَسْبَابٍ: أَنْ يَتُوبَ فَيَتُوبُ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ فَإِنَّ التَّائِبَ مِنْ الذَّنْبِ كَمَنْ لَا ذَنْبَ لَهُ. أَوْ يَسْتَغْفِرُ فَيُغْفَرُ لَهُ أَوْ يَعْمَلُ حَسَنَاتٍ تَمْحُوهَا فَإِنَّ الْحَسَنَاتِ يُذْهِبْنَ السَّيِّئَاتِ. أَوْ يَدْعُو لَهُ إخْوَانُهُ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ وَيَسْتَغْفِرُونَ لَهُ حَيًّا وَمَيِّتًا. أَوْ يَهْدُونَ لَهُ مِنْ ثَوَابِ أَعْمَالِهِمْ مَا يَنْفَعُهُ اللَّهُ بِهِ أَوْ يَشْفَعُ فِيهِ نَبِيُّهُ مُحَمَّدٌ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ. أَوْ يَبْتَلِيهِ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى فِي الدُّنْيَا بِمَصَائِبَ تُكَفِّرُ عَنْهُ أَوْ يَبْتَلِيهِ فِي الْبَرْزَخِ بِالصَّعْقَةِ فَيُكَفِّرُ بِهَا عَنْهُ. أَوْ يَبْتَلِيهِ فِي عَرَصَاتِ الْقِيَامَةِ مِنْ أَهْوَالِهَا بِمَا يُكَفِّرُ عَنْهُ. أَوْ يَرْحَمُهُ أَرْحَمُ الرَّاحِمِينَ.
