He replied, “Yes.” He said, “Do not do that, for if you do, your eyes will become sunken and you will grow exhausted.” He then instructed him to fast three days each month. He replied, “I can manage more than that.” Eventually, he instructed him to fast on alternate days. He said, “I can manage more than that.” He replied, “There is nothing better than that.” He also said:

“The best fasting is the fasting of David, peace be upon him: he would fast one day and not fast the next, and he would not flee when he met the enemy. The best night prayer is that of David: he would sleep half the night, pray for a third of it, and sleep for a sixth.”

He instructed him to recite the Quran in seven days.

Since these were the familiar forms of worship, he said in the hadith concerning the Khawārij recorded in the two Sahīh collections:

“Any one of you would consider his prayer insignificant compared with theirs, his fasting compared with theirs, and his recitation compared with theirs. They recite the Quran, but it does not go beyond their throats. They pass out of the religion as an arrow passes through its quarry.”

He thus mentioned their strenuous devotion to prayer, fasting, and recitation, and that they go to such extremes in these that the Companions would consider their own worship insignificant beside theirs.

These people went to excess in worship without understanding, which ultimately led them into religious innovation. He therefore said:

“They pass out of Islam as an arrow passes through its quarry. Wherever you find them, kill them, for whoever kills them will have a reward with Allah on the Day of Resurrection.”

For they had deemed it lawful to shed the blood of Muslims and declared those who disagreed with them to be disbelievers. Hadiths have been transmitted concerning them

that are authentic. Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah Most High have mercy on him, said, “The hadith concerning them has been authentically transmitted through ten routes.” Muslim included these in his Sahīh, and al-Bukhārī included some of them.

These three kinds of worship are prescribed; the question that remains, however, concerns the prescribed extent of each. It was on this subject that the Book of Moderation in Worship was written. Ubayy ibn Kaʿb and others said:

“Moderation in following the Sunnah is better than strenuous devotion to innovation.”

The question concerning fasting continuously, fasting throughout the year except for the two Eid days and the days of Tashrīq, and spending the entire night in prayer is whether this is recommended—as a group of jurists, Sufis, and devout worshippers have held—or disliked, as the Sunnah indicates, even if permissible. Yet fasting on alternate days is better, and praying for a third of the night is better. A detailed discussion of this belongs elsewhere.

The purpose here is to discuss kinds of worship that are not prescribed and that arose among later generations, such as retreats in seclusion, which resemble the prescribed retreat in the mosque. The prescribed retreat in mosques, as practised by the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and his Companions, is indeed one of the prescribed acts of worship. As for retreats in seclusion, some cite his devotional worship in the Cave of Hirā’ before revelation as evidence for them, but this is a mistake;

for whatever he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did before prophethood, we are commanded to follow him in it if he prescribed it after prophethood; otherwise, we are not. From the time Allah Most High made him a prophet, he never again ascended to the Cave of Hirā’, nor did his Rightly Guided Caliphs. He, may Allah’s blessings be upon him, lived in Mecca for a little over ten years before the Hijrah. He entered Mecca for the make-up ‘umrah, stayed there for nearly twenty nights in the year of the Conquest, and came there for the Farewell Pilgrimage, staying for four nights. Although the Cave of Hirā’ was nearby, he did not visit it.

People used to visit this cave during the pre-Islamic period of ignorance. It is said that ‘Abd al-Muttalib instituted this practice among them, because they did not have the prescribed acts of worship that he, may Allah’s blessings be upon him, brought after prophethood, such as prayer and devotional retreat in mosques. These dispense with the need to visit Hirā’, unlike their situation before revelation began. For he did not read; rather:

“The angel, peace be upon him, said to him, ‘Read.’ He, may Allah’s blessings and peace be upon him, said, ‘I replied, “I cannot read.”’”

Nor did they know this prayer. Thus, when the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, performed it, some polytheists, such as Abū Jahl, forbade him from doing so. Allah Most High said:

“Have you seen the one who forbids
A servant when he prays?
Have you seen if he is upon guidance
Or enjoins righteousness?
Have you seen if he denies and turns away?
Does he not know that Allah sees?
No! If he does not desist, We will surely drag him by the forelock—
A lying, sinful forelock.
Then let him call his associates;
We will call the angels of Hell.
No! Do not obey him, but prostrate and draw near.”

And “a group” make the retreat in seclusion forty days long and attach great importance to this forty-day observance.

and they argue in its support that Allah Most High appointed thirty nights for Moses, peace be upon him, and completed them with ten more. It is also reported that Moses, peace be upon him, fasted throughout them, and that the Messiah likewise fasted forty days for Allah Most High and was spoken to afterward. They therefore say that after this period one is spoken to and receives visitations, just as they say that revelation descended after the retreat in the Cave of Hirā’.

This too is mistaken, for this practice is not part of the religious law of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Rather, it was prescribed for Moses, peace be upon him, just as the Sabbath was prescribed for him, whereas Muslims do not observe the Sabbath. Likewise, certain things were forbidden under his law that were not forbidden under the law of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Thus, the former argument appeals to an abrogated law, while the latter appeals to a practice preceding prophethood.

Experience has shown that those who engage in these innovated acts of worship are visited by devils and receive demonic visitations and communications. Some are carried through the air by their devils. I know a number of these people who sought visitations of the kind received by the prophets, but devils descended upon them because they had departed from the law of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, which they had been commanded to follow.

Allah Most High said:

“Then We set you upon a prescribed way in matters of religion, so follow it, and do not follow the desires of those who do not know.

“They will be of no help to you whatsoever against Allah. The wrongdoers are allies of one another, while Allah is the Protector of the righteous.”

Many of them prescribe neither a particular place nor a particular duration for seclusion, but simply instruct a person to withdraw into seclusion.

Then, some practitioners of seclusion came to adhere to prescribed forms of worship: prayer, fasting, Quran recitation and remembrance of Allah. Most, however, depart into forms that have not been prescribed. One example is the method of Abū Hāmid and his followers. They instruct the person in seclusion to do nothing beyond what is obligatory: no recitation, no study of prophetic hadith, nor anything else. Instead, they may instruct him to engage in remembrance, and may then repeat what Abū Hāmid says:

“The remembrance of ordinary people is: ‘There is no god but Allah.’ The remembrance of the elite is: ‘Allah, Allah.’ The remembrance of the elite of the elite is: ‘He’ ‘He.’”

Invoking the name alone, whether explicitly or through a pronoun, is an innovation in religion and an error in speech and language. A bare name does not constitute a statement and expresses neither faith nor disbelief.

It is authentically established that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The best words after the Quran are four, and they are themselves found in the Quran: Glory be to Allah; praise be to Allah; there is no god but Allah; and Allah is the Greatest.”

Another hadith states:

“The best remembrance is: ‘There is no god but Allah.’”

He also said:

“The best thing that I and the prophets before me have said is: ‘There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner. To Him belongs all sovereignty, and to Him belongs all praise, and He has power over all things.’”

There are many authentic hadiths concerning the virtues of these words. As for invoking the name alone, this is an innovation that has not been prescribed. It is not intelligible speech, nor does it contain any expression of faith. For this reason, some later proponents of this practice have come to explain that it is not

translated_text:
they may even say that he receives something of the same kind as the prophets receive. Some of them claim to have received more than the prophets received. Abū Hāmid frequently praises this method in al-Ihyā and elsewhere, just as he praises asceticism to excess. This reflects the lingering influence of philosophy upon him. For philosophers such as Ibn Sīnā and others like him claim that all knowledge received in the hearts of prophets and others comes solely from the active intellect.

For this reason, they say that prophethood can be acquired: when a person frees himself from distractions, his heart—according to them—becomes pure, and something of the same kind as flowed into the hearts of the prophets flows into his heart. They hold that Moses son of ‘Imrān, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was spoken to from the heaven of his own intellect; he did not hear speech from outside himself. They therefore say that they receive the same as Moses received, or something even greater.

Abū Hāmid says that he heard the address just as Moses, peace be upon him, heard it, even though he himself was not its intended recipient. All this stems from their deficient faith in the messengers, and from their believing in some of what the messengers brought while disbelieving in other parts. What they have said is false on several grounds:

First: What they call the “active intellect” is false and has no reality, as has been explained at length elsewhere.

Second: What Allah places in hearts sometimes comes through the mediation of angels

when it is true, and at other times through the mediation of devils when it is false. Angels and devils are living, speaking beings, as abundant evidence conveyed by the prophets establishes, and as those versed in spiritual realities who have encountered them directly also claim. Yet these philosophers maintain that angels and devils are merely attributes of the human soul. This is grave misguidance.

Third: Angels came to the prophets with revelation from their Lord. Among them were those to whom Allah Most High spoke, drawing them near and calling to them, as He spoke to Moses, peace be upon him. What they received was not merely an emanation, as these people claim.

Fourth: If a person empties his heart of every thought, how can he know that what enters it is true? This could only be known through reason or revelation, and neither provides evidence for that.

Fifth: What is known through revelation and reason is that when a person empties his heart of everything, devils dwell within it and then descend upon him, just as they used to descend upon soothsayers. What prevents Satan from entering a human being’s heart is the remembrance of Allah within it, with which He sent His messengers. When the heart is devoid of that remembrance, Satan takes charge of it. Allah Most High says:

“Whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We assign to him a devil to be his companion. The devils surely turn them away from the path, while they think they are rightly guided.”

And Satan said, as Allah relates:

“He said, ‘By Your might, I will surely lead them all astray, except Your servants among them

“You have no authority over My servants, except those of the misguided who follow you.”

Those who are chosen are those who worship Him alone, associating nothing with Him. Allah is worshipped only in the manner He has commanded through His messengers; whoever does otherwise falls under the control of devils. This is an area in which many spiritual wayfarers have fallen into grave error: they have confused spiritual states bestowed by the Most Merciful with satanic states. They have experienced things like those experienced by soothsayers and sorcerers, imagining them to be miracles granted to Allah’s pious friends. This has been discussed at length elsewhere.

Sixth: Even if this method were sound, it could apply only to someone to whom no messenger had come. But when a messenger has come to someone and he has been commanded to follow a particular path, whoever opposes that messenger goes astray. The last of the messengers, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, commanded his community to perform prescribed acts of worship, including prayer, remembrance, supplication, and recitation. He never commanded them to empty their hearts of every thought and wait for whatever might descend upon them.

Even supposing this method had been followed by some prophets, it would have been abrogated by the law brought by Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Rather, the emptying and clearing of the heart taught by the Messenger means emptying it of what Allah does not love and filling it with what He loves. One empties it of worship of anything other than Allah and fills it with worship of Allah. Likewise, one empties it of love for anything other than Allah and fills it with love for Allah; removes from it fear of anything other than Allah and instils in it fear of Allah Most High; and removes reliance upon anything other than Allah and establishes reliance upon Allah within it.

This is Islam, which encompasses faith—a faith that the Quran nourishes and strengthens, rather than contradicts and negates. As Jundub and Ibn ʿUmar said:

“We learned faith, then learned the Quran, and so increased in faith.”

As for confining oneself to prescribed remembrance alone, such as saying, “There is no god worthy of worship but Allah,” a person may sometimes benefit from this. Yet this remembrance alone, to the exclusion of everything else, is not the path to Allah Most High. Rather, the best bodily act of worship is prayer, followed by recitation of the Quran, then remembrance, then supplication. An otherwise lesser act, performed at its prescribed time, is better than a superior act. Thus, glorifying Allah while bowing and prostrating is better than reciting the Quran, and supplication at the end of prayer is likewise better than recitation.

Moreover, a person may find doors opened to him through a lesser deed that are not opened to him through a superior one. One deed may also be made easy for him while another is not, so the former is better for him because he is unable to perform the superior deed. This is like a hungry person who finds inferior bread readily available while better bread is difficult to obtain

Seventh:

Abū Hāmid likens this to the work of Chinese and Byzantine artisans in decorating a wall: one group polished their wall until it reflected what the other group had polished. This analogy is unsound, because the person who emptied his heart had no other heart through which his own could acquire adornment, as one wall acquires it from the other. Rather, he says that knowledge is inscribed in the celestial soul, which he calls “the Preserved Tablet,” following Ibn Sīnā.

We have explained elsewhere that “the Preserved Tablet” mentioned by Allah and His Messenger is not the celestial soul. Ibn Sīnā and his followers took terms found in the revealed Law and assigned them referents different from those intended by the one who brought that Law. They then began using these terms, leading the uninformed to suppose that they intended the same meanings as the one who brought the Law. Thus, they took the kernel of philosophy and clothed it in the husk of the revealed Law. Examples include the terms “mulk” (dominion), “malakūt” (sovereignty), “jabarūt” (might), “the Preserved Tablet,” “angel,” “devil,” “coming into existence,” “beginninglessness,” and others.

Among the things they prescribe are hunger, sleeplessness, and silence, together with seclusion, without any limits set by the revealed Law. such as the reports concerning the sevenfold recitations (al-musabbaʿāt), which he narrated from al-Khidr, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. These are pure falsehood, even though they contain nothing but Quran recitation. He also sometimes mentions innovated acts of worship, such as the excessive praise of hunger offered by him, Abū Hāmid, and others. They describe weighing bread against moist wood, so that the amount eaten decreases as the wood dries. They also cite accounts of prayers for the various days and nights, all of them false and fabricated. Alongside this, they may therefore mention some corrupt imaginings. This is not the place to discuss that at length.

The purpose here is simply to draw attention to a category of innovated worship: “innovated retreats,” whether their duration is fixed or not. They involve innovated acts of worship: either practices whose general kind is prescribed but for which no fixed measure has been laid down, or practices whose very kind is not prescribed. As for lawful retreat, withdrawal, and solitude, these are whatever has been commanded as obligatory or recommended.

(The former) includes withdrawing from forbidden matters and avoiding them, as Allah Most High says:

“When you see those who speak offensively about Our verses, turn away from them until they engage in some other discourse.”

This also includes His words concerning His intimate friend:

“When he withdrew from them and from what they worshipped besides Allah, We granted him Isaac and Jacob, and made each of them a prophet.”

And His words concerning the people of

the Cave:

“Now that you have withdrawn from them and from what they worship other than Allah, take refuge in the cave.”

Those men were not in a place where Friday or congregational prayers were held, nor was there anyone who enjoined adherence to a prophet’s revealed law. That is why they took refuge in the cave. Moses also said:

“If you do not believe in me, then leave me alone.”

As for withdrawing from people when it comes to superfluous permissible pursuits and things of no benefit, by renouncing such things, this is recommended. Tāwūs said: “What an excellent hermitage a man’s home is, where he restrains his gaze and hearing!”

If someone wishes to attain proficiency in knowledge or practice and therefore seeks solitude somewhere while continuing to attend Friday and congregational prayers, this is right. Thus, it is related in the two Sahīh collections that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was asked, “Who is the best of people?” He replied:

“A man who holds the reins of his horse in Allah’s cause: whenever he hears a cry of alarm, he rushes towards it, seeking death wherever it is likely to be found; and a man who lives apart in a mountain valley, establishes prayer, gives zakat, and leaves people alone except to do good.”

His words, “establishes prayer and gives zakat,” indicate that this man possesses wealth on which he pays zakat, and that he lives among people, giving the call to prayer among them, with prayer established in their midst. For the Prophet, may Allah’s blessings be upon him, said:

“There are no three people in a village or in the desert among whom prayer is not established in congregation but that Satan has gained mastery over them.”

He also said:

“Keep to the congregation, for the wolf devours only the sheep that strays away.”

Section

Those who undertake these “retreats” may seek out places where neither the call to prayer nor the announcement of its commencement is made, and where there is no mosque in which the five daily prayers are offered. These may be abandoned mosques or places other than mosques, such as caves and caverns in the mountains, graveyards—especially the grave of someone held in high regard—or places said to contain a trace of a prophet or a righteous man. Consequently, they undergo satanic experiences in these places which they imagine to be miraculous gifts bestowed by the Most Merciful.

Some of them see the occupant of a grave coming to them, although he has been dead for many years, and saying, “I am so-and-so.” He may even say, “When we are placed in the grave, we come out,” as happened to al-Tūnisī with Nu‘mān al-Salāmī.

Devils frequently assume human form, both in waking life and in dreams. They may approach someone who does not recognize them and say, “I am Shaykh so-and-so,” or “I am the scholar so-and-so.” Sometimes they say, “I am Abū Bakr,” or “I am ‘Umar.” A devil may even appear while someone is awake rather than dreaming and say, “I am the Messiah,” “I am Moses,” or “I am Muhammad.” I know of various occurrences of this kind.

translated_text:
And there are those who believe that the prophets appear in their own forms to people who are awake. There are also shaykhs known for asceticism, learning, scrupulousness and religious devotion who believe such things. Some of them imagine that when they visit a prophet’s grave, the prophet emerges from it in his own form and speaks to them.

Some have seen the figure of a shaykh in the area around the top of the Kaaba and said that it was Abraham, the intimate friend of Allah. Others imagine that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, has come out of his burial chamber and spoken to them. They count this among their own miraculous gifts. Some believe that if they ask the person buried in a grave a question, he answers them.

Some used to relate that whenever Ibn Mandah found a hadith difficult to understand, he would go to the Prophet’s burial chamber, enter it and ask the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, about it, and he would answer him.

Another man from the Maghreb had a similar experience and counted it among his miraculous gifts. Ibn ‘Abd al-Barr therefore said to someone who believed this:

“Alas for you! Do you consider this man superior to the earliest forerunners among the Emigrants and the Helpers? Did any of them question the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, after his death and receive an answer? The Companions disagreed over various matters; why, then, did they not ask the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and receive his answer? Here was his own daughter Fātimah disputing over his inheritance; why did she not ask him and receive his answer?”

وَلَا يَجُوزُ أَنْ يُقَالَ إنَّ هَذَا مُسْتَحَبٌّ أَوْ مَشْرُوعٌ إلَّا بِدَلِيلِ شَرْعِيٍّ وَلَا يَجُوزُ أَنْ يُثْبِتَ شَرِيعَةً بِحَدِيثِ ضَعِيفٍ لَكِنْ إذَا ثَبَتَ أَنَّ الْعَمَلَ مُسْتَحَبٌّ بِدَلِيلِ شَرْعِيٍّ وَرُوِيَ لَهُ فَضَائِلُ بِأَسَانِيدَ ضَعِيفَةٍ جَازَ أَنْ تُرْوَى إذَا لَمْ يُعْلَمْ أَنَّهَا كَذِبٌ وَذَلِكَ أَنَّ مَقَادِيرَ الثَّوَابِ غَيْرُ مَعْلُومَةٍ فَإِذَا رُوِيَ فِي مِقْدَارِ الثَّوَابِ حَدِيثٌ لَا يُعْرَفُ أَنَّهُ كَذِبٌ لَمْ يَجُزْ أَنْ يُكَذَّبَ
translated_text:
Section

We have been commanded to believe in what the prophets—may Allah’s blessings and peace be upon them all—were given, and to follow them and their guidance. Allah Most High says:

“Say: We believe in Allah and what has been revealed to us, and what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob and the Tribes, and what Moses and Jesus were given, and what the prophets were given by their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and to Him we submit.”

Allah Most High also says:

“Those are the ones whom Allah has guided, so follow their guidance.”

Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, is the Seal of the Prophets; there is no prophet after him. His law has abrogated those parts of earlier prophets’ laws that it supersedes. Thus, no path to Allah remains except through following Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. Whatever acts of worship he commanded, whether as obligations or recommendations, are prescribed in religion. The same applies to whatever he encouraged and whose reward and merit he mentioned.

It is not permissible to declare something recommended or prescribed in religion without evidence from revelation, nor is it permissible to establish a religious ruling on the basis of a weak hadith. However, if an act has been established as recommended through evidence from revelation, and reports describing its merits are transmitted through weak chains, those reports may be narrated provided they are not known to be false. This is because the amounts of reward are unknown. Thus, if a hadith concerning the amount of reward is transmitted and is not known to be false, it is not permissible to reject it as false

translated_text:
, and this is what Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal and others permitted, along with narrating hadiths concerning the merits of deeds.

But that they would establish, on the basis of a weak hadith, that an act is recommended and prescribed in religion—Allah forbid! Likewise, when they knew that a hadith was false, they did not consider it permissible to narrate it without explaining that it was false, because the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said in an authentic hadith:

“Whoever narrates a hadith from me, believing it to be false, is one of the liars.”

Whatever the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, did as an act of worship is worship in which following his example is prescribed. If he singled out a particular time or place for an act of worship, then singling it out for that worship is Sunnah. Examples include his singling out the last ten nights for spiritual retreat and the Station of Abraham for prayer. Following his example means doing what he did, in the manner he did it, because he did it. This is only achieved by intending the same purpose that he intended. Thus, if he travelled for Hajj, ʿumrah, or jihad, and we travel for the same purpose, we are following him. The same applies when he struck someone to carry out a prescribed punishment. This is unlike someone who travelled as he did but had a different purpose, or struck as he did but had a different purpose: such a person is not following him.

If, however, he did something incidentally—such as stopping at a place during a journey, pouring water left in his waterskin at the base of a tree, or his mount walking along one side of the road, and similar things—is it recommended to deliberately follow his example in that? Ibn ʿUmar liked to

 مَا هَذَا؟

translated_text:
do such things. The Rightly Guided Caliphs and the majority of the Companions, however, did not regard this as recommended, because it does not constitute following his example. Following his example necessarily involves intention: if he did not intend that particular action, but it occurred merely by chance, then deliberately doing it does not constitute following his example.

Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, maintained that even if the Prophet had not intended it, the act itself was good, however it occurred, and so he liked to do the same—either because this increased his love for him or because of the blessing of resembling him. This includes giving dates as zakāt al-fitr when dates are not one’s staple food. Ahmad agreed with Ibn Umar on such matters and permitted actions like those Ibn Umar performed. Likewise, following Ibn Umar, Ahmad permitted rubbing one’s hand over the place where the Prophet sat on the pulpit.

Two positions are reported from Ahmad concerning rubbing one’s hand over the pulpit. The better-known position is that it is disliked, as the majority hold. Mālik and other scholars disliked these practices even though Ibn Umar performed them, since the leading Companions, such as Abū Bakr, Umar, Uthmān and others, did not do so.

It is established through an authentic chain of transmission that Umar ibn al-Khattāb, may Allah be pleased with him, was travelling when he saw people frequenting a place to pray there. He asked, “What is this?”

They replied, “A place where the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, prayed.”

He said, “Do you wish to turn the sites associated with your prophets into places of worship? This is precisely what destroyed those before you. Whoever happens to be there when prayer is due should pray there; otherwise, let him continue on his way.”

Likewise, scholars hold two views concerning the permissible acts he performed without any particular intent: is imitating him in these acts merely permissible, or is it recommended? Both views are found in the school of Ahmad and elsewhere, as has been explained in detail in its proper place. Neither Ibn Umar nor any other Companion would deliberately seek out the places where he stayed or spent the night, such as his wives’ houses or his encampments during military expeditions. The discussion concerned only resembling him in the outward form of an action, even when he had not intended it as an act of worship. As for the places themselves, the Companions agreed that none should be venerated except those venerated by the Lawgiver.

Section

As for those who practise “innovated acts of worship,” Satan makes these acts seem attractive to them and makes them dislike the ways prescribed by Islamic law. Eventually, he makes them averse to religious knowledge, the Quran and hadith, so that they dislike hearing the Quran and hadith or having them mentioned. He may even make them averse to books themselves, so that they dislike any book and anyone carrying one, even if it is a copy of the Quran or a collection of hadith.

Thus, al-Nasrābādhī related that they used to say, “He abandons the knowledge of patched cloaks and takes up the knowledge of written pages!” He said, “I used to hide my writing tablets from them, but when I grew older, they needed my knowledge.”

Likewise, al-Sarī al-Saqatī related that one of them came to see him, but when he saw an inkwell and a pen beside him, he left without sitting down with him. This is why Sahl ibn Abd

Allah al-Tustarī said:

“O Sufis, do not abandon black ink on white paper, for no one has abandoned black ink on white paper without falling into heresy.”

Al-Junayd said:

“This knowledge of ours is founded upon the Book and the Sunnah. Whoever has not read the Quran and written down hadith is not to be followed in this matter.”

Many of these people recoil from anyone who mentions Islamic law or the Quran, carries a book, or writes. This is because they have sensed that such material contains things that contradict their way. Their devils therefore drive them away from it, just as a Jew or a Christian keeps his son from hearing what Muslims say, lest his beliefs about his religion change, and just as Noah’s people would put their fingers in their ears and cover themselves with their garments so that they would neither hear his words nor see him.

Allah Most High said of the polytheists:

“Those who disbelieve say, ‘Do not listen to this Quran, but make noise during its recitation, so that you may prevail.’”

He Most High also said:

“Why, then, do they turn away from the reminder, like startled wild donkeys fleeing from a lion?”

They are among those most eager for innovated listening practices—listening to musical instruments—and among those least inclined toward the listening prescribed by Islamic law: listening to the verses of Allah Most High.

One thing that made their way seem attractive to them was finding many of those occupied with religious knowledge and books turning away from worshipping Allah Most High and following His path, whether through preoccupation with worldly affairs, involvement in sins, or ignorance and denial of what those devoted to Allah and His worship attain. The presence of such people thus helped to alienate them, and a kind of mutual hatred developed between the two groups, resembling

in some respects, that between the adherents of the two faiths: one group says, “The other has no sound foundation,” and the other says, “They have no sound foundation.”

They may think that through their path they attain something greater than what can be attained through books. Some imagine that they can learn the Quran without being taught. They relate that someone attained this, but this is false. He may, however, have heard Allah’s verses and then, after purifying his soul, remembered and recited them. Spiritual discipline refines the soul, enabling a person to recall things he had forgotten.

Some of them say—or it is related that one of them said:

“They took their knowledge from one dead man transmitting from another, whereas we took our knowledge from the Ever-Living, who never dies.”

This does occur. Yet some of them imagine that whatever is imparted to them, whether words addressed to them or a thought arising within them, comes directly from Allah Most High, without an intermediary, when it may come from Satan. They have no criterion by which to distinguish what comes from the Most Merciful from what comes from Satan. The unfailing criterion is the Quran and the Sunnah: whatever accords with the Book and the Sunnah is true, and whatever contradicts them is erroneous.

Allah Most High has said:

“Whoever turns away from the reminder of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil to be his companion. These devils turn them away from the path, while they think they are rightly guided. Then, when he comes to Us, he says, ‘If only there were between you and me the distance between east and west! What an evil companion!’”

The reminder of the Most Merciful is what He revealed to His Messenger. Allah Most High said:

“This is a blessed reminder which We have sent down.”

He Most High also said:

“It is nothing but a reminder to all the worlds.”

And He Most High said:

“When guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor suffer. But whoever turns away from My remembrance will have a life of hardship, and We will raise him blind on the Day of Resurrection. He Most High also said:

“Indeed, this Quran guides to what is most upright and gives glad tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a great reward, and that for those who do not believe in the Hereafter We have prepared a painful punishment.”

He Most High also said:

“And thus We have revealed to you a revelation by Our command. You did not know what the Book was, nor what faith was, but We have made it a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants. And indeed, you guide to a straight path—the path of Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on earth. Surely, to Allah all matters return.”

He Most High also said:

“A Book We have sent down to you so that you may bring people out of darkness into light, by their Lord’s permission, to the path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy.”

He Most High also said:

“So those who believe in him, honour him, support him, and follow the light sent down with him—it is they who will prosper.”

Then, because these people imagined that this came to them from Allah without an intermediary, they came to regard themselves as above following the Messenger. One of them says:

He also says:

“So-and-so takes his knowledge from the Book, whereas this shaykh takes his from Allah,” and similar things.

These states may be satanic, or they may come from the Most Merciful. There must therefore be a criterion by which to distinguish the allies of the Most Merciful from the allies of Satan. That criterion is none other than the Criterion with which Allah sent Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. For He is:

“the One who sent down the Criterion upon His servant, that he might be a warner to the worlds.”

It is through this that Allah has distinguished truth from falsehood, guidance from misguidance, right conduct from waywardness, the path to Paradise from the path to Hell, and the way of the allies of the Most Merciful from the way of the allies of Satan. Such an experience may also be caused by listening to musical instruments. This is like what is related from ‘Uthmān ibn ‘Affān, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said:

“Beware of wine, for it is the mother of all evils. A man propositioned a woman, and she said, ‘I will not agree until you prostrate before this idol.’ He replied, ‘I will not associate partners with Allah.’ She said, ‘Then will you kill this boy?’ He replied, ‘I will not take a life that Allah has forbidden.’ She said, ‘Then will you drink this cup?’ He replied, ‘This is less serious.’ But when he drank the wine, he killed the boy, prostrated before the idol, and committed fornication with the woman.”

Musical instruments are the wine of souls: they affect souls more powerfully than potent wine does. When people become intoxicated by sounds, associating partners with Allah takes hold of them, and they incline toward sexual immorality and injustice. Thus they associate partners with Allah, take lives that Allah has forbidden them to take, and commit fornication. These three things are common among those who listen to musical instruments—to whistling and clapping. As for associating partners with Allah, it predominates among them: they love their shaykh or someone else as they love Allah, and become ecstatic in their love for him.

As for “sexual immorality,” singing is an incantation that invites fornication and is among the greatest causes of sexual immorality. A man, a boy, or a woman may be exceptionally chaste and dignified until attending such a gathering. Then their restraint dissolves, sexual immorality becomes easy for them, and they incline toward it, whether as the active or passive partner, or both—just as happens among wine-drinkers, and even more so.

As for “killing,” they frequently kill one another during listening sessions. They say, “He killed him through his spiritual state,” and count this as evidence of his power. In fact, devils accompany them and attend their gatherings; whoever has the stronger devils kills the other. They are like people who drink wine with supporters around them: once they drink, they become belligerent, and whoever has the stronger supporters kills the other. Such things have happened to many of them. Some kill a person, a horse, or something else through their spiritual state. Then someone seeking vengeance appeals to his shaykh for help, and the shaykh kills that person along with a group accompanying him—perhaps ten, fewer, or more. Such incidents have happened to more than one person.

The ignorant used to consider this a form of (miraculous gifts). But when it became clear that these were satanic states, and that these people had devils helping them in sin and aggression, those whom Allah Most High granted insight recognized the truth, and these people’s deception and fraud were exposed.

“For a vow brings the son of Adam to what has been decreed.”

The vow prohibited here is one that must nevertheless be fulfilled: making it is prohibited, but once a person has made it, he must fulfill it. Thus, in Sahīh al-Bukhārī, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever vows to obey Allah, let him obey Him; and whoever vows to disobey Allah, let him not disobey Him.”

He, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prohibited making vows because doing so brings no benefit beyond binding oneself to what one has undertaken, which one may then be unwilling to fulfill and thus remain sinful.

It would be better for a person to perform those acts of worship without making a vow. People intend through vows to obtain what they seek, but the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, explained that vows bring no good. A vow is therefore not a means of obtaining what they seek. For example, someone making a vow might say, “If Allah enables me to memorize the Quran, I pledge to Allah that I will fast three days,” or, “If Allah cures me of this illness, repels this enemy, or settles this debt for me, I will do such-and-such.” He has thereby made the act of worship he has undertaken an exchange for what he seeks.

Yet Allah, glorified is He, does not fulfill that need merely because of the vowed act of worship. Rather, He grants His servant what he seeks to test whether he will be grateful or ungrateful. Gratitude to Him consists in doing what He has commanded and refraining from what He has forbidden. As for that vowed act of worship, it does not suffice as gratitude for that blessing. Yet the person making this vow may have neglected many of Allah’s rights, then offered that vow in return for that blessing. Likewise, Allah Most High has made charity and other acts of worship means of obtaining good and warding off evil when the servant performs them on his own initiative.

As for what he does by way of a vow, it neither brings him benefit nor wards off harm. Rather, he was miserly, but once he made the vow, fulfilling it became binding upon him. Thus, through vows Allah Most High extracts something from the miser: he gives because of the vow what he would not have given without it. And Allah knows best.

Shaykh al-Islām—may Allah have mercy on him—was asked:

“What are the deeds of the people of Paradise, and what are the deeds of the people of Hell?”

He replied:

All praise is due to Allah, Lord of all worlds.

“The deeds of the people of Paradise” are faith and piety, while the deeds of the people of Hell are disbelief, wickedness, and disobedience.

The deeds of the people of Paradise include believing in Allah, His angels, His Books, His messengers, and the Last Day; believing in the divine decree, both its good and its evil; bearing the two testimonies—that none has the right to be worshipped except Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah; establishing prayer; paying zakat; fasting Ramadan; and performing pilgrimage to the Sacred House. They also include worshipping Allah as though you see Him, for although you do not see Him, He sees you.

Among “the deeds of the people of Paradise” are speaking truthfully, fulfilling trusts, keeping covenants, being dutiful to parents, maintaining ties of kinship, and showing kindness to neighbours, orphans, the needy, and those in one’s possession, whether human slaves or animals.

“Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, He will admit them into Gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great triumph.”

“And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and transgresses His limits, He will admit him into a Fire, abiding therein forever, and he will have a humiliating punishment.”

And Allah knows best.

translated_text:
The Shaykh—may Allah have mercy on him—said:

Section

As for his question, “Is seclusion or mixing with others better for someone following the spiritual path?”—although people dispute this “question,” either in general terms or with reference to particular circumstances, the truth is that “mixing with others” is sometimes obligatory or recommended. The same person may be instructed to mix with others at one time and to remain alone at another.

The governing principle is this: if “associating with others” involves cooperation in righteousness and piety, it is enjoined; if it involves cooperation in sin and transgression, it is forbidden. Thus, joining Muslims in acts of worship—such as the five daily prayers, Friday prayer, the two Eid prayers, the eclipse prayer, the prayer for rain, and similar acts—is among the things Allah and His Messenger have commanded. The same applies to joining them in Hajj and in military expeditions against the disbelievers and the renegade Khawārij, even if those leading these activities are wicked, and even if there are wicked people among those assembled.

A servant must also have times alone for supplication, remembrance of Allah, prayer, reflection, self-examination, setting his heart right, and attending to personal matters in which no one else shares. These require solitude, whether at home—as Tāwūs said, “What an excellent hermitage a man’s home is: there he restrains his gaze and his tongue”—or elsewhere. To favour mixing with others unconditionally is therefore mistaken, as is favouring solitude unconditionally. How much each person needs of either, and what is best for him in each circumstance, requires individual consideration, as explained earlier.

The same applies to “taking practical means and foregoing them.” Whoever is able to take such means without being distracted from what is more beneficial to his religion is commanded to do so while placing his trust in Allah. This is better for him than accepting from others, even if something comes to him without his asking. For such a person, taking these means is an act of worship of Allah, and he is commanded to worship Allah and put his trust in Him. If, however, he takes these means without a righteous intention, or does not put his trust in Allah, then he is [not] (1) obedient in these two respects, and this is [not] (2) the way of the prophets and the Companions. Pursuing the activity in which he is more obedient is what is prescribed for him. This varies according to people’s circumstances.

As explained earlier, what is best varies “sometimes” according to the category of worship: prayer as a category is better than Quran recitation, Quran recitation is better than remembrance of Allah, and remembrance of Allah is better than supplication.

“Sometimes” it varies according to the time: after Fajr and Asr, Quran recitation, remembrance of Allah, and supplication are prescribed rather than prayer.

“Sometimes” it varies according to the outward act a person is performing: during bowing and prostration, remembrance of Allah and supplication are prescribed rather than Quran recitation. Likewise, remembrance of Allah and supplication during circumambulation are prescribed by scholarly agreement, whereas Quran recitation during circumambulation is a matter of well-known disagreement.

“Sometimes” it varies according to the place: at Arafah, Muzdalifah, the stoning sites, and Safā and Marwah, remembrance of Allah and supplication are prescribed rather than prayer and similar acts. For someone arriving in Mecca, circumambulating the House is better than prayer, whereas for residents of Mecca, prayer is better.

The shaykh also said:

All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. May Allah bless him and grant him abundant peace.

To proceed:

Know that every sane adult, whether human or jinn, must bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. He sent him with guidance and the religion of truth to make it prevail over all other religions, and sufficient is Allah as a witness.

He sent him to all creation: humans and jinn, Arabs and non-Arabs, Persians, Indians, Berbers, Romans, and all other non-Arab peoples, black and white. By non-Arabs is meant those who are not Arabs, whatever their languages.

Muhammad—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—was sent to everyone among humans and jinn, whether People of the Book or otherwise, concerning every inward and outward matter of religion: its beliefs, realities, paths, and laws. There is no creed but his creed, no reality but his reality, no path but his path, and no religious law but his religious law. No created being can reach Allah or attain His good pleasure, His Paradise, or the honor He bestows

and His friendship except by following him inwardly and outwardly in words and deeds: in the heart’s affirmations and beliefs, its states and realities, the speech of the tongue, and the actions of the limbs. No one is a close friend of Allah unless he follows him inwardly and outwardly, believing what he has reported about the unseen and committing himself to obeying him in what he has enjoined upon creation: fulfilling obligations and abstaining from prohibitions.

Whoever does not believe what he has reported and commit himself to obeying what he has made obligatory and commanded, both in the inward matters of the heart and in outward bodily actions, is not a believer, let alone a close friend of Allah, however extraordinary the feats he may perform. If he neglects to do what is commanded and to abstain from what is forbidden—including fulfilling obligations such as prayer and other duties, with their requisite purification and obligatory elements—then his states can only be satanic states, which distance him from Allah and bring him nearer to His wrath and punishment.

As for children and the insane who are not religiously accountable, the pen of accountability has been lifted from them, so they are not punished. They do not possess the inward and outward faith in Allah and piety that would place them among Allah’s pious close friends, His successful party, and His victorious forces. They are, however, included within Islam by virtue of their parents’ affiliation, as the Most High says:

“And those who believe and whose descendants follow them in faith—We will join their descendants with them, without diminishing the reward of their deeds in any way. Every person is held in pledge for what he has earned.”

Yet, lacking reason, they cannot be among those whose hearts possess the realities of faith, the knowledge of Allah’s close friends, and the spiritual states of His chosen servants, for all these things depend upon reason. Insanity is incompatible with reason, assent, knowledge, certainty, guidance, and praise. Allah raises in rank only those who believe and those who have been given knowledge. Thus, although Allah does not punish the insane person and shows him mercy in the Hereafter, he is not among Allah’s close friends—those brought near to Him and those who follow a middle course—whose ranks Allah raises.

Whoever believes that any of these people who neither fulfil their obligations nor abstain from prohibitions—whether sane, insane, bereft of their senses, or lost in bewilderment—is among Allah’s pious close friends, His successful party, His righteous servants, His victorious forces, the foremost who are brought near to Him, and those who follow a middle course, whose ranks Allah raises through knowledge and faith, despite that person neither fulfilling his obligations nor abstaining from prohibitions: whoever believes such a person to be a close friend of Allah is a disbeliever who has apostatized from Islam. He does not bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace; rather, he denies what Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, has testified to.

For Muhammad reported from Allah that Allah’s close friends are the pious believers. The Most High says:

“Indeed, the close friends of Allah will have no fear, nor will they grieve—”

“Those who believed and were mindful of Allah.”

And the Most High says:

“O mankind, We created you from a male and a female and made you into peoples and tribes so that you may know one another. Indeed, the most honourable of you in Allah’s sight is the most pious of you.”

And “piety” means obeying Allah, guided by light from Allah and hoping for His mercy, and refraining from disobedience to Allah, guided by light from Allah and fearing His punishment. A close friend of Allah draws near to Him only by fulfilling the obligatory duties, then performing voluntary acts of worship. Allah Most High says:

“My servant has not drawn near to Me through anything like fulfilling what I have made obligatory upon him. My servant continues to draw near to Me through voluntary acts of worship until I love him.”

This is related in the authentic divine hadith narrated by al-Bukhārī.

Section

Among the deeds most beloved to Allah and the greatest obligations in His sight are the five daily prayers at their prescribed times. They are the first deeds for which a servant will be called to account on the Day of Resurrection. Allah Most High Himself made them obligatory on the night of the Ascension, placing no intermediary between Himself and Muhammad in this matter. Prayer is the pillar of Islam, without which it cannot stand, and the most important matter of religion. As the Commander of the Faithful, ʿUmar ibn al-Khattāb, used to write to his officials:

“The most important of your affairs in my eyes is prayer. Whoever observes it and maintains it faithfully preserves his religion. Whoever neglects it will neglect his other deeds even more.”

It is authentically reported in the Sahīh that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Between a servant and associating partners with Allah lies the abandonment of prayer.”

He also said: “The covenant between us and them

Whoever does not believe that prayer is obligatory upon every sane person who has reached puberty, except women who are menstruating or experiencing postnatal bleeding, is a disbeliever and an apostate, by agreement of the leading scholars of the Muslims. Even if he believes that it is a righteous deed which Allah loves and rewards, and he himself prays, stands in prayer at night, and fasts during the day, yet does not believe it obligatory upon everyone who has reached puberty, he is likewise a disbeliever and an apostate until he believes that it is a binding obligation upon every sane person who has reached puberty.

Whoever believes that this obligation is waived for certain shaykhs who possess spiritual knowledge, receive unveilings, and have attained their goal; or that Allah has an elect upon whom prayer is not obligatory, but from whom its obligation has been lifted because they have reached the Sacred Presence, or because something more important or more worthy renders them independent of it; or that the purpose is for the heart to be present with the Lord; or that prayer disperses one's attention, so that when a servant is wholly concentrated upon Allah, he has no need of prayer—rather, the purpose of prayer is spiritual knowledge, and once that is attained, he no longer needs prayer, for the aim is for you to perform an extraordinary feat, such as flying through the air, walking on water, filling vessels with water from the air, making waters sink away and extracting the treasures beneath them, or killing someone he hates through satanic states, so that once he achieves this, he has no further need of prayer—and other such notions; or that Allah has certain members of His elect who do not need to follow Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, but have become independent of him just as al-Khidr was independent of Moses; or that every

person who receives unveilings and flies through the air or walks on water is a friend of Allah, whether he prays or not; or believes that prayer is accepted without ritual purification; or regards as friends of Allah the ecstatics, the enraptured, and the insane who frequent cemeteries, rubbish dumps, tahārāt, inns, qamāmīn, and other such places, neither performing ablution nor offering the obligatory prayers—whoever believes that these people are friends of Allah is a disbeliever and an apostate from Islam, by agreement of the leading scholars of Islam, even if he himself is an ascetic devoted to worship.

Monks are even more ascetic and devoted to worship. They believe in much of what the Messenger brought, and most of them revere the Messenger and his followers. Yet they have not believed in everything he brought; rather, they have believed in some and disbelieved in some, thereby becoming disbelievers. As Allah Most High says:

“Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers and wish to distinguish between Allah and His messengers, saying, ‘We believe in some and disbelieve in others,’ and wish to adopt a way in between—

“Those are the disbelievers, truly. And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.

“But those who believe in Allah and His messengers and make no distinction between any of them—to those He will give their rewards. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.”

As for someone deprived of reason or insane, the most that can be said is that he is exempt from accountability and therefore incurs no punishment. His faith, prayer, fasting, and all his other deeds are invalid, for no deeds are accepted without reason. Thus, anyone who lacks reason

has no valid acts of worship, whether obligatory or voluntary. Whoever has neither obligatory nor voluntary acts of worship is not among the friends of Allah.

For this reason, Allah Most High says:

“Indeed, in that are signs for those of understanding.”

That is, those who possess reason. Allah Most High also says:

“Is there not in this an oath sufficient for a person of understanding?”

That is, a person of reason. Allah Most High says:

“And fear Me, O people of understanding.”

He also says:

“Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are the deaf and dumb who do not reason.”

And Allah Most High says:

“Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Quran so that you may understand.”

Allah praises and commends only those who possess reason. As for those who lack reason, Allah has neither praised nor commended them, nor has He ever spoken favourably of them. Rather, Allah Most High says of the people of the Fire:

“And they will say, ‘If only we had listened or reasoned, we would not be among the companions of the Blaze.’”

Allah Most High also says:

“And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind. They have hearts with which they do not understand, eyes with which they do not see, and ears with which they do not hear. They are like livestock; rather, they are more astray. It is they who are heedless.”

And He says:

“Or do you think that most of them hear or reason? They are only like livestock; rather, they are even further astray.”

Thus, anyone who lacks reason has neither valid faith nor valid obligatory or voluntary worship. If someone was a Jew or a Christian, then became insane and embraced Islam after becoming insane, his acceptance of Islam is valid neither inwardly nor outwardly. If someone had believed, then disbelieved and subsequently became insane, he is subject to the same ruling as disbelievers. Some Quran commentators have said—and this is reported from al-Dahhāk—“Do not approach prayer while you are stupefied with sleep.” This interpretation holds if the verse is understood to indicate this by inference or through the inclusive meaning of its general wording. Otherwise, there is no doubt that the occasion of the verse’s revelation concerned intoxication from wine, and its wording explicitly indicates that. The other meaning is also sound.

It is authentically reported in the two Sahīh collections that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“When one of you rises to pray at night and his tongue falters in reciting the Quran, let him sleep, for he does not know: he may intend to seek forgiveness but instead curse himself.” In another wording: “If he rises to pray and becomes drowsy, let him sleep.”

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, thus forbade praying when drowsiness causes a person to make mistakes. The scholars have cited this as evidence that drowsiness does not invalidate ablution. Were ablution invalidated by it, the prayer would become invalid, or one would have to leave it to renew one’s ritual purification. Yet the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, explained the reason only by saying:

“For he does not know: he may intend to seek forgiveness but instead curse himself.”

It is therefore clear that he intended to forbid prayer for someone who does not know what he is saying, even when this is caused by drowsiness.

Abū al-Dardā’ said:

“A sign of a man’s understanding is that he first attends to his needs, then turns to his prayer with an unoccupied heart.”

If prayer is forbidden whenever a person is deprived of reason—even through something permissible—until he knows what he is saying, then it is all the more clearly impermissible for an insane person to pray, or anyone who falls within that designation, even if described as distraught or bewildered.

It is well known that prayer is “the finest act of worship,” as reported in the two Sahīh collections from Ibn Masʿūd, who said:

“I asked the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, ‘Which deed is most beloved to Allah?’

“He replied, ‘Prayer at its appointed time.’

“I asked, ‘Then which?’

“He replied, ‘Dutifulness to one’s parents.’

“I asked, ‘Then which?’

“He replied, ‘Striving in Allah’s cause.’”

Ibn Masʿūd said: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, told me these things, and had I asked him for more, he would have told me more.”

It is also authentically reported in the two Sahīh collections that he ranked faith in Allah and striving in His cause as the best deeds, followed by an accepted Hajj.

There is no contradiction between the two reports, for prayer is included within the meaning of faith in Allah, just as it is included in His words, Most High:

“Allah would never let your faith go to waste.”

Al-Barā’ ibn ʿĀzib and others among the early generations said: “That is, your prayers facing Jerusalem.”

If he is incapable of performing any of its actions and cannot utter its words, should he pray by moving his eyes and mentally recalling its actions? Scholars hold two views on this, though the stronger view is that this is not prescribed.

Thus, it becomes clear that someone who has lost his reason has been deprived of the obligatory and voluntary acts through which he might draw near to Allah. “Friendship with Allah” consists of faith and piety, which entail drawing near to Him through obligatory and voluntary acts. He has therefore been deprived of the means by which Allah’s friends draw near to Him. Nevertheless, while insane, he is exempt from accountability and is not punished, just as children and animals are not punished, since they bear no religious responsibility in this condition.

If, before the onset of insanity, he was a believer who performed righteous deeds and drew near to Allah through obligatory and voluntary acts, he retains the reward for that previous faith and righteous conduct. His share of friendship with Allah Most High remains commensurate with the faith and piety he possessed, just as this is not lost through death. This differs from apostasy from Islam, for apostasy nullifies deeds. No sin other than apostasy nullifies righteous deeds, just as no good deed other than repentance wipes out all sins.

During his insanity, however, he is not credited with the equivalent of the deeds he used to perform when lucid, just as no equivalent of his previous misdeeds is recorded against him when his reason is absent through intoxicating practices or sleep. This is because, in this condition, he has no sound intention. However, in the hadith

which is authentic and narrated by Abū Mūsā, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“When a servant falls ill or travels, he is credited with the deeds he used to perform while healthy and resident.”

It is also authentically reported that during the expedition to Tabūk, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“There are men in Medina who have been with you on every journey you have made and in every valley you have crossed.” They asked, “Even though they are in Medina?” He replied, “Even though they are in Medina. A valid excuse has kept them back.”

These people intended and wished to continue the deeds they used to perform, but were unable to do so. They therefore attained the same standing as those who performed them. This differs from someone who has lost his reason, for he has neither a sound intention nor any worship at all, whereas those people have a sound intention for which reward is recorded.

If, however, before becoming insane, he was a disbeliever, openly disobedient, or sinful, the onset of insanity does not erase his previously established disbelief and disobedience. Thus, Jews and Christians who become insane after embracing Judaism or Christianity will be gathered with their respective communities. Likewise, Muslims who become insane after having faith and piety will be gathered with the pious believers.

Losing one’s reason through insanity or otherwise—whether the person is described as overwhelmed or bewildered—does not increase one’s faith or piety. Nor does the loss of reason cause any increase in one’s goodness, righteousness, or sin. Rather, insanity deprives a person of reason, leaving him with whatever good and evil he already possessed, neither increasing nor diminishing it. His insanity, however, deprives him of further good, just as it prevents him from being punished for evil.

If, however, a person loses his reason through something forbidden—such as drinking wine or consuming hashish, attending melodious singing and listening until he loses his reason, engaging in innovated acts of worship until some devils attach themselves to him and impair his reason, or taking henbane that deprives him of reason—such people deserve blame and punishment for what they have done to deprive themselves of reason.

Many of these people induce a satanic state by doing what pleases them: dancing wildly until they lose their reason, or snorting and bellowing until the satanic state comes upon them. Many deliberately seek bewilderment until they become deranged. All these people belong to Satan’s party, and such conduct is known of more than one of them.

The scholars have disagreed over whether they remain “subject to religious obligations” while deprived of reason. The underlying issue is “the case of an intoxicated person.” The explicitly transmitted position of al-Shāfi‘ī, Ahmad, and others is that such a person remains subject to religious obligations while deprived of reason. Many scholars, however, hold that he is not; this is one of the two positions within the schools of al-Shāfi‘ī and Ahmad. One of the two reports from Ahmad also holds that a divorce pronounced by an intoxicated person does not take effect. This is the stronger of the two views.

None of the scholars has said that those who lose their reason through such means thereby become Allah’s close allies, devoted to His oneness, or members of His successful party. As for those among the ‘wise madmen’ whom the scholars have mentioned favorably, they belong to the first category: those who possessed goodness before losing their reason.

Among the “signs of such people” is that, if they experience some lucidity during their madness, they speak of the faith in their hearts, not disbelief and falsehood. This contrasts with others who, upon regaining some awareness, speak words of disbelief and association of partners with Allah, and babble words of disbelief while deprived of reason. Such a person is a disbeliever, not a Muslim.

As for those who babble unintelligibly in Persian, Turkish, Berber, or other languages—as happens to some who attend gatherings for devotional singing and experience an ecstasy that overwhelms their reason until they babble unintelligibly, or speak in a language other than Arabic—it is Satan who speaks through their tongues, just as he speaks through the tongue of someone possessed.

If someone says that Allah gave these people reason and spiritual states, then preserved their states while taking away their reason, and relieved them of the obligations He had imposed upon them because of what He took away, the response is:

Your statement, “Allah bestowed spiritual states upon them,” is ambiguous. Such states fall into two categories: states from the Most Merciful and satanic states. Whatever extraordinary phenomena these people experience, such as disclosures of hidden matters and astonishing powers of action, may “at times” be of the same kind as those experienced by sorcerers and soothsayers, and “at other times” come from the Most Merciful, like those experienced by people of piety and faith.

If, while in possession of their reason, these people had gifts arising from faith and were pious believers, then there is no doubt that, upon losing their reason, they are relieved of religious obligations because their reason has been taken away. But if what they were given consisted of satanic states—such as those granted to polytheists, the People of the Book, and hypocrites—then losing their reason does not remove them from their previous disbelief and wickedness, just as the former are not removed from their previous faith

and piety. Likewise, for anyone in either group, sleep, death, or unconsciousness does not, through the loss of reason, alter the standing established by his previous faith and obedience or disbelief and wickedness. At most, it removes religious obligations.

Exemption from accountability entails neither praise nor commendation nor reward. Losing his reason does not earn a person any gift bestowed upon Allah’s friends or any miraculous favor granted to the righteous. Rather, he is simply exempted from accountability, just as someone asleep, unconscious, or dead is exempted. There is neither praise nor blame in this. Indeed, someone asleep is in a better condition than these people. Thus, the prophets, peace be upon them, slept, but none of them was insane or mentally deranged. Sleep and unconsciousness can occur to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, but insanity cannot. Our Prophet Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would sleep with his eyes while his heart remained awake, and he lost consciousness during his illness.

As for “insanity,” Allah has kept His prophets free of it, for it is among the gravest human deficiencies: human perfection lies in reason. This is why Allah has forbidden impairing reason by any means and has forbidden whatever leads to its impairment, such as drinking wine. He has forbidden even a drop of it, although it does not impair reason, because it leads to drinking a large quantity that does impair it. How, then, could losing one’s reason be a cause of friendship with Allah, a condition for it, or something that brings one closer to it, as many misguided people imagine—so much so that one of them said of these people:

translated_text:
“They are a people who have cast off order and breached … the bounds: for them there is neither obligatory nor voluntary worship.
Madmen—yet the secret of their madness … is so exalted that reason prostrates at its gates.”

These are the words of a misguided man—indeed, a disbeliever—who imagines that a madman possesses a secret at whose threshold reason prostrates. This is because he has witnessed in some madmen a kind of disclosure of hidden matters or an astonishing feat beyond the ordinary. Such things occur because of the devils associated with the madman, just as they occur with sorcerers and soothsayers. This misguided man therefore imagines that anyone who discloses hidden matters or performs extraordinary feats is a friend of Allah.

Whoever believes this is a disbeliever by the consensus of Muslims, Jews, and Christians. For many disbelievers and polytheists, let alone the People of the Book, experience disclosures of hidden matters and extraordinary feats through their devils many times greater than those experienced by these people. The further a man strays and the greater his disbelief, the closer Satan is to him. Yet all these people’s disclosures necessarily contain lies and fabrications.

Their deeds must likewise involve wickedness and transgression, just as do those of their brethren among sorcerers and soothsayers. Allah Most High says:

“Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend?”

“They descend upon every sinful liar.”

Thus, anyone upon whom the devils descend must be marked by lying

and wickedness, whatever group he belongs to. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, explained that Allah’s friends are those who draw near to Him through obligatory acts of worship: His successful party, His victorious army, and His righteous servants.

Whoever believes that someone who performs neither obligatory nor voluntary acts of worship—whether because he lacks reason, is ignorant, or for some other reason—is one of Allah’s pious friends; whoever regards such people as Allah’s pious friends, His successful party, and His righteous servants, is a disbeliever who has apostatized from the religion of the Lord of all worlds. If he says, “I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah,” he is among the liars of whom it is said:

“When the hypocrites come to you, they say, ‘We bear witness that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah.’ Allah knows that you are indeed His Messenger, and Allah bears witness that the hypocrites are certainly liars.”

“They have taken their oaths as a shield and have turned people away from the way of Allah. Evil indeed is what they have been doing.”

“That is because they believed, then disbelieved, so their hearts were sealed, and they do not understand.”

It is authentically reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever neglects three Friday prayers out of carelessness, without an excuse, Allah will seal his heart.”

If the heart of someone who abandons Friday prayers is sealed even though he performs the noon prayer, what, then, of someone who performs neither the noon prayer nor the Friday prayer, neither obligatory nor voluntary prayers, and does not purify himself for prayer, whether by the full ritual bath or by ablution? Such a person, if he had previously been a believer and his heart had been sealed, would be a disbeliever and an apostate because of the obligations he abandoned and did not believe to be obligatory. If someone believes him to be a believer, that person is a disbeliever and an apostate. How, then, can he be considered one of the friends of

Allah who are mindful of Him?

Allah Most High has said, describing the hypocrites:

“Satan has gained mastery over them and made them forget the remembrance of Allah.”

That is, he has taken control. The expression hādha al-ibila hawdhan means “he drove the camels along.” As for those over whom Satan has gained mastery, driving them to oppose what Allah and His Messenger have commanded, Allah Most High says:

“Do you not see that We have sent the devils against the disbelievers, inciting them relentlessly?”

That is, stirring them up violently. These are the people of whom He says:

“Satan has gained mastery over them and made them forget the remembrance of Allah. They are Satan’s party. Indeed, Satan’s party are the losers.”

In the Sunan collections, Abū al-Dardā’ reports that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whenever there are three people in a village among whom neither the call to prayer is made nor the prayer established, Satan gains mastery over them.”

Thus, any three of these people among whom neither the call to prayer is made nor the prayer established belong to Satan’s party, over whom he has gained mastery—not to the friends of the Most Merciful whom He has honoured. This remains so even if they are devoted worshippers and ascetics who practise hunger, sleeplessness, silence and seclusion, like the monks in monasteries and those who dwell in caves and caverns: the people of Mount Lebanon, Mount al-Fath at Asūn, Mount Laysūn, and the Cave of Blood on Mount Qāsiyūn, and other mountains and places frequented by many ignorant, misguided worshippers. There they undertake retreats and ascetic exercises without the call to prayer being made or the five daily prayers being established among them. Rather, they engage in acts of worship that neither Allah nor His Messenger has prescribed. They worship Him according to their own spiritual tastes and experiences, without assessing their states against the Quran and Sunnah
